name: Core Engine
intro: You are the Creator at the dawn of a cosmos. Your sons are gods with their own passions, grudges and domains, and each of them is a real AI agent. After every move the gods make, the deterministic world engine takes over and runs fifty years of history. Mortals are born, love, betray and die. Peoples migrate, languages split, harvests fail, plagues spread, empires overreach. Then Fate judges the epoch and writes the chronicle.

governs.title: A living world
governs.text: More than 400 simulation steps for mortals, population, settlements, ecology, climate, disasters, plagues, trade, markets, production, factions, institutions, diplomacy, espionage, war, faith, spirits, magic, heroes, monsters, realms, the afterlife, the gods and the sky.

governs.title: Gods who think
governs.text: God cards across 7 rarity tiers, from Common to Mythic. More than a hundred divine tools in 13 families: reading, memory, language, lineage, prayer, creation, resources, influence, knowledge, intervention, war, death and the cosmos. Loyalty, ambition, wrath and mercy drive every god's decisions. Gods can die and be brought back. Even a mortal can be deified and join the pantheon.

governs.title: 47 divine domains
governs.text: From sea to fire, from storm to memory, from oath to sleep. Each domain bends the world in its own way, and each one has a price.

governs.title: The council of the gods
governs.text: Even gods must vote. Even gods scheme.

governs.title: Fate and the chronicle
governs.text: The impartial judge of every epoch. Verdicts, canon facts, open story hooks and prophecies that come true. Bard and deepener agents turn raw history into legend and epic. Every people tells the story of the gods in its own voice.

governs.title: Living languages
governs.text: Procedural languages with dialects, contact, change and death. Every name has a meaning, every word a history.

governs.title: Prayers and revelations
governs.text: Mortals pray to the gods, dream of them, threaten them. The gods answer.

governs.title: 44 record types
governs.text: From regions to species, from peoples to legends, from armies to prophecies. Each one is a living part of the simulation, with its own values, bonds, chronicle and portrait.

governs.title: The cosmos
governs.text: Real astronomy and pure fantasy share one sky. Each of the 32 star types sets the warmth, the harvest and the sanity of everyone beneath it. 23 branches of knowledge and 32 creature traits decide what the world can know and what it will meet.

governs.title: The interface
governs.text: More than thirty screens, from the pantheon to the chronicle, from the live map to the 3D cosmos and the knowledge graph. Every value is editable, and everything updates live.

governs.title: Images
governs.text: A local image service paints the Creator, the gods, the worlds and every being from descriptions the agents write.

motto: One Creator, divine sons and a world that lives on its own.

name: The Loom
intro: The Loom is the heart of the product and the ground the other 99 expansions stand on. Its job is to make every system in the universe talk to every other. A drought does not just cut the harvest: at the same moment it moves prices, migration, faith, the logistics of war and a god's reputation. The Loom records each of these effects, keeps its cause and knows whose hand it came from.
outcome: There is not one number in your universe without an explanation, not one event without a known cause, and not one corner your hand cannot reach.

governs.title: Every influence on record
governs.text: Every influence on a value, whether a wound, a law, a feast, a curse or the season's weather, is kept separately and then combined. Hover over any number and you read what set it, by how much and for how long.

governs.title: Cause and effect
governs.text: Every war, death, betrayal and discovery is recorded with its cause, its participants and its place. Events link into chains, and history can be traced backwards by person, by place or by kind of event.

governs.title: The books of the universe
governs.text: People, goods, money, souls and divine power are counted one by one at every step. Every transfer has a source and a destination. Any loss or surplus that cannot be explained is caught as an error.

governs.title: Links between systems
governs.text: What every mechanic reads and writes is on record. Every value one system produces is used by another. No value exists only to be stored.

governs.title: Full control
governs.text: Every mechanic answers to 6 commands: run it now, pause it for a set time, edit the records it controls, retune its rules, pin a value in place and lock a record against the simulation. All of it can be undone.

governs.title: Harshness setting
governs.text: Heroic, realistic or brutal. A single setting decides together how deadly wounds, infection, plague, famine, childbirth and siege hunger are. Every rate beneath it can also be tuned on its own.

governs.title: Parallel engine
governs.text: Worlds are computed in parallel and their results merged in a fixed order. One core or many, the result is the same. Quiet regions and sleeping mortals are not computed until something touches them.

depth.text: Every subsystem affects every other subsystem.
Between the economy and society alone, for example, there are 384 separate one-way links.
The engine reads and processes 778 separate properties of a mortal, 1,205 of a people and 1,359 of a settlement.
Every mechanic's table, steps, controls, interface screen, agent tools and chronicle line are registered in a compliance catalogue. A mechanic missing any one of them cannot enter the product.

name: Turning Seasons
intro: Turning Seasons turns epochs from abstract blocks of time into years that are lived. Inside every epoch the engine runs real years and seasons, so every event has a place on the calendar: harvests sprout in spring, armies march in summer, famine strikes in winter. The same storm hits a fleet, an army's advance, a market's prices and a god's reputation all at once.
outcome: "the third winter of the war" or "the year of hunger" is no longer decoration but the universe's own record.

governs.title: Seasons
governs.text: Every world's seasons come from its own sky: axial tilt, moons and world type. Ice worlds live through a long winter and a short thaw, and tidally locked worlds have no seasons at all. You can add or remove seasons and change the values of each one.

governs.title: Long, irregular seasons
governs.text: On worlds with chaotic orbits, a winter or a summer can last for years. A long season can be caused by the orbit, by a law of nature or by a god. A people's scholars can see a long winter coming, as far as their reckoning and their instruments allow. Peoples who heed the warning prepare, and cities with granaries and famine foods come through the winter with fewer losses.

governs.title: Weather
governs.text: Weather is drawn for every region in every season. It affects visibility, footing, cold, heat, wetness, wind, morale and growth separately. A fog makes an ambush possible, a blizzard breaks a siege, wind spreads a city fire. You can force any weather you like on any region.

governs.title: Years and campaign rounds
governs.text: The years inside an epoch are processed one by one. Campaigns move through real seasons, market prices rise and fall with the season, and plagues spread in the warm months.

governs.title: Years to remember
governs.text: The worst years of famine, plenty, weather and plague in every epoch get a name, enter the chronicle and can become legend.

governs.title: Calendars
governs.text: Every people keeps its own calendar: sowing, harvest, midwinter, campaign season and holy days. A calendar can count from a ruler's accession, a city's founding or a god's descent. Holy days are tied to the seasons and to the years people remember.

governs.title: Moons and tides
governs.text: The number of moons sets the strength of the tides and how often eclipses come. Year length, day length and the number of seasons follow from the world's physics, and you can change all of them.

depth.text: Between 1 and 8 seasons per world.
Any world can have 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8 seasons.
Each society names its seasons in its own way.

depth.label: Every season carries one of 7 warmth states

depth.text: 25 kinds of weather, from clear skies to void rain and from sandstorms to auroras, each with 11 separate effects.
5 seasonal water states.
4 ways a season can arrive.
Irregular long winters and summers that can arise from 8 causes, with 5 different reaches.
10 kinds of named year, among them famine, plenty, weather and plague.
14 kinds of calendar slot
2 shapes of long season
Long season shapes: cycling or single.
16 kinds of effect from calendar slots and traditions

name: The Living Land
intro: The Living Land turns the map from a picture into a real place. Every region carries its soil, rainfall, temperature, forests, rivers and past. The land never forgets what happens on it: felled forests give way to erosion, overworked fields to exhaustion, abandoned villages to returning woodland. Ground where a great battle or a massacre took place grows dark, and ground where a saint lies buried becomes holy.
outcome: The geography of your universe changes along with its history, and every region has a past to tell.

governs.title: Region profile
governs.text: Every region's terrain, soil, temperature band, rainfall, seasonality, river, coast, water source, minerals, disease burden, passability and defensibility. All of it comes from the map itself.

governs.title: Land use and ecological pressure
governs.text: Clearing forests, working fields, grazing, mining and building. These lead to erosion, soil exhaustion, desertification and disease. Abandoned land returns from grassland to scrub and from young forest to old forest, until a wildfire starts the cycle again.

governs.title: The memory of the land
governs.text: Wars, massacres, sacks, disasters, plagues, famines, the deaths of gods, the burials of saints and miracles all leave a mark on a region. Dark memories curse it, holy memories light it up. Some memories fade with time, others last forever.

governs.title: Scars
governs.text: Battlefields, salted earth, craters, cursed and haunted places, plundered plains, earthworks, military roads and broken bridges. Scars outlive the people who made them and touch every harvest taken from that land.

governs.title: Dangers
governs.text: Creatures, bandits, monsters, natural phenomena, disease, avalanches, quicksand and volcanoes. Each danger strikes settlers, herds, travellers, armies and merchants in its own way. In winter avalanches close the passes, in spring floods fill the valleys, in summer wildfires break out. An army that marches into an unmapped region can lose its way.

governs.title: Places and their secrets
governs.text: Named places, from mountain peaks to passes and from sacred groves to the corpses of gods. A place can hide secret resources, buried relics, sealed spirits, lost knowledge, lost rites or an entrance to the underworld. Explorers, seers and miners find them and bring them to light.

governs.title: Ley lines
governs.text: Neighbouring regions rich in magic are joined by lines that carry magic storms and strengthen the temples and gates built on them. Where lines meet, the nodes become holy places and targets of war.

governs.title: Changing geography
governs.text: Droughts turn land into desert, great floods move riverbeds, salt spreads through the soil. The gods can shape the land too: raise mountains, work the soil, redirect rivers. Peoples see it, and come to admire or fear their gods for it.

depth.text: 34 kinds of terrain, from steppe to crystal field and from living flesh to void shore, and 19 kinds of soil, from lime to bone.
10 ways of moving, from walking to flying to burrowing through the ground. Each one crosses every terrain with its own difficulty.
19 kinds of scar and 16 kinds of memory the land keeps
15 sources of danger with 11 separate targets, and 10 kinds of seasonal terrain hazard.
48 kinds of place and 15 kinds of secret a place can hide.
A natural cycle of 12 stages, from bare ground to old forest and swamp forest.
19 kinds of terrain trait
5 kinds of movement medium

name: Stone and Deep
intro: Stone and Deep adds depth to the universe, quite literally. Beneath every region lies a column of stone you can read layer by layer, and beneath that lie caverns, a magma sea and the realm of the dead. The deeper miners dig, the richer the veins they reach, and the greater the risk: collapsing galleries, flooding shafts and caverns full of beings never seen on the surface. Rivers live with a real flow, the crust moves, and coasts advance or retreat over generations. The traces of past ages lie hidden deep in the ground as well.
outcome: What lies beneath your universe becomes as rich a source of stories as its surface.

governs.title: The geological column
governs.text: Beneath every region lie ordered layers of rock, born of the world's crustal movement and volcanism, each with its own thickness and veins. Deep layers hide rarer ores, and hard rock demands better tools. Limestone and sandstone hold water and form caves, and marble makes grand buildings possible.

governs.title: Underground strata
governs.text: Aquifers that feed the wells; three cavern layers, each a world of its own with its own species, fungus forests and cave peoples; on volcanic worlds, a magma sea that feeds the foundries; and at the very bottom, the realm of the dead. Deep digs break into the caverns, bring their species and peoples to light and release creatures onto the surface.

governs.title: Mining dangers
governs.text: The depth of the dig, the hardness of the rock and the miners' engineering knowledge set the yearly risk of collapse and flooding. A collapse crushes miners, closes the shaft and sometimes opens a cavern.

governs.title: Seals
governs.text: Walls, warding rites and a god's hand close off the depths that have been opened. Every seal wears down over time, the beings below press against it, and miners can dig their way past it.

governs.title: Rivers and waters
governs.text: Flow born of upstream rainfall and the season, navigability, salt in the estuaries, and floodplains. Snowmelt in the mountains brings spring floods. Dams and canals built upstream can leave the realm downstream without water, and a water dispute becomes a cause for war. Great floods, earthquakes, the gods or you can move a river's bed.

governs.title: Earthquakes and volcanoes
governs.text: Plate boundaries, formed together with the map, decide where quakes and eruptions happen. Eruptions darken the sky with ash, enrich the soil and can build new land.

governs.title: Sediment and coasts
governs.text: Rivers, wind, ice, waves and slopes carry sediment. Sediment builds deltas and marshes, makes floodplains fertile, fills harbours and canals, and buries settlements and finds. Coasts advance or erode over generations: an eroding coast swallows fields and buildings, and an advancing one leaves harbours stranded inland.

governs.title: The record of deep time
governs.text: Fossil beds hold the remains of extinct species, giant beasts, slain monsters, earlier creations and vanished peoples. Mines, digs, floods and quakes bring them to light. Every people reads its finds through its own knowledge: proof of a legend, a holy relic or evidence of deep time. Organic beds turn into coal and oil, and well-preserved remains make it possible to bring extinct species back.

depth.text: 28 kinds of rock, from soil to crystal bedrock, with layers of frozen methane, bone and glass on stranger worlds.
11 underground strata in all, among them a magma sea and the realm of the dead.
7 kinds of seal, among them structures, rites and divine power.
10 causes that can move a riverbed
6 sediment carriers and 10 kinds of sediment. 13 coast forms, from cliff to fjord and from delta to ice shelf.
8 sources of fossils, 8 ways to read them and 8 kinds of preservation, from rock to amber and from ice to tar.

name: Winds of the World
intro: Winds of the World gives the universe's climate a physical logic. Winds, rains, currents and climate eras are no longer random values but consequences of a world's spin, tilt, light and geography. Deserts form where mountains catch the rain, and fertile coasts form where cold water wells up. The warming of a distant ocean can touch the harvests of two realms that have never heard of each other, in the very same year.
outcome: Every forest, desert and fertile coast on your map stands somewhere you can explain, and climate becomes a force that changes the course of history.

governs.title: Prevailing winds
governs.text: Every world's spin, light and air pressure set its wind belts: trade winds, westerlies and polar winds. Slowly turning worlds form a single belt, on worlds locked to their star the wind blows from the lit face, and on worlds without an atmosphere the air is still. Wind draws the sea lanes, fans wildfires and carries foul air to the lands downwind.

governs.title: Rain shadows
governs.text: Moist sea wind drops its rain on the windward slopes of mountains, and the lands behind them dry out. Every region's rainfall follows this reckoning.

governs.title: Monsoons
governs.text: Once a year a monsoon reaches the coasts of the warm latitudes, and its strength changes from year to year. A strong monsoon eases the sea lanes and enriches the coastal towns. A monsoon that never comes becomes a named year of hunger, drags down the prosperity of the coastal towns and puts the sea lanes at risk.

governs.title: Ocean currents
governs.text: Warm currents ease the sea lanes, and coasts where cold water wells up become rich fishing grounds. Currents carry news and rumour from one shore to another and bring living species to new coasts.

governs.title: Climate oscillations
governs.text: Worlds with seas swing between warm, neutral and cold phases. These swings change the rainfall and temperature of the warm latitudes, bringing drought or flood to distant lands in the same years. The seers of peoples who read the sky can see them coming.

governs.title: Regional climate
governs.text: Every region's temperature depends on its world's star, its sea current and its climate era. Supernovae and volcanic eruptions can cool whole worlds. Gods can change a region's climate, turn the winds and stir up monsoons.

governs.title: A breathing planet
governs.text: Carbon, water and nutrients move between volcanoes, forests, oceans, rivers and soil. The carbon cycle sets the air, the water cycle the rain and the seas, the nutrient cycle the fertility of the soil. A planet whose forests are burned, or on which a god imposes an endless summer, answers as a whole over the epochs.

depth.text: 12 kinds of wind belt, from trade winds to still air.
6 kinds of current, from warm to cold.
5 oscillation phases.
11 climate eras, from temperate to ice age and from drought to scorching heat.

name: Plough and Net
intro: Plough and Net turns the question of how a people feeds itself from a matter of economics into a matter of history. Fields, vineyards, pastures and fisheries run on hidden stocks that are spent or restored over generations. Irrigation without drainage salts a civilization's lands over the centuries, enclosed common pastures push peasants into the cities, and an overfished ground one day yields nothing at all.
outcome: You can trace the roots of famines, migrations and social movements back to the land itself.

governs.title: Market towns and farming rings
governs.text: Settlements form tiers by daily, weekly and rare needs. New settlements rise where the gaps between markets call for them. Around every town, gardens, woods, grain fields, pastures and wilds lie in rings. A new road or canal pushes those rings outward.

governs.title: Farming intensifies
governs.text: Crowded land drives peoples to irrigation, terraces, crop rotation and manuring, while empty land holds the change back. Peoples who remember famine develop famine foods and granaries.

governs.title: The hidden stocks of the soil
governs.text: Every field's yield depends on four stocks: a nitrogen-like element, minerals, organic matter and salt. Crops drain these stocks, and legumes, fallow, manure, floods and ash restore them.

governs.title: Plantings that last generations
governs.text: Orchards, vineyards, groves and timber forests mature over years or epochs and bring their owners a return. An enemy who cuts them down scars a land for generations.

governs.title: The commons
governs.text: Common pastures, woods and fisheries are kept by good custom or by a council, and collapse under overuse. Rulers can enclose them: the owners grow rich, and peasants left without land move to the cities.

governs.title: Fisheries and hunting grounds
governs.text: Fish stocks, trapping, fowling and the hunt for great sea creatures. The catch grows with the gear and the labour put in. A ground that falls below its collapse line yields nothing and recovers very slowly. Closed seasons, protected waters, catch quotas and gear bans save grounds, and wardens hold back poaching.

governs.title: Herding
governs.text: Grazing, milking, shearing, eggs and slaughter, breeding seasons and herd sizes, oxen that pull the plough, and animals trained for war, the hunt and guarding.

depth.text: 7 farming rings, from gardens to wilds, and 6 tiers of market.
6 hidden stocks beneath every field.
9 kinds of long-lived planting, from orchards to timber forests.
12 kinds of commons and 7 ways to govern them
10 kinds of catch ground and 12 kinds of gear, from line to harpoon.

name: Wild Kingdoms
intro: Wild Kingdoms takes living species off the encyclopedia page and sets them down on the land. Every species lives region by region, breeds in its own season, eats what it can find and moves along its migration routes. Species depend on one another through a food chain: a predator whose prey runs out turns on the herds, and the loss of a sacred species throws a faith into crisis. Plants live at the same depth, with their bodies, their seasons and the yields they give.
outcome: The nature of your universe is a living system that shapes the economy, faith and history of its peoples directly.

governs.title: Ranges
governs.text: Every species has its own population in every region. It grows with fertility, habitat, temperature and food, and shrinks with hunters, predators, disease and farming. Migratory species move between regions with the season.

governs.title: Diets and traits
governs.text: Diets from herbivore to scavenger, and creatures that feed on sunlight, stone, souls or the void. Some thirty traits, from echolocation to camouflage and from eating iron to breathing fire, decide what each species can do.

governs.title: The food chain
governs.text: Who hunts whom is worked out again every epoch from diet, size and shared habitat. You can pin or forbid any feeding link.

governs.title: Domestication
governs.text: Wild species are first tamed, then herded, domesticated and finally bred into breeds. Domestic lines grow gentler and more productive, and become mounts and war beasts. Populations kept apart from the rest split into highland and desert lines.

governs.title: Pests
governs.text: Crop pests cut the harvest, iron eaters gnaw at the ore, disease carriers spread plague, and the vermin that spoil the granaries only stop once an animal that hunts them is domesticated.

governs.title: Plants
governs.text: Crops, medicinal herbs, dyes, timbers, brewing plants, magic reagents and poisons are living plants with seasons, soils and pests. Every plant has a body, from root to seed and from bark to sap, and its yields come from those parts. Its growth form sets the time to its first harvest and how badly storms and fire will hurt it.

governs.title: Pets and companions
governs.text: A dog by the hearth eases loneliness, and its death leaves real grief. Falcons and war dogs strengthen the hunt and the battle.

depth.text: 12 classes of living species

depth.label: 7 size classes from tiny to colossal, 15 diets and 8 social structures

depth.text: 9 biochemistries, from carbon and water to silicon and from crystal to spirit.
8 stages of domestication, from wild to breed, and 19 uses, from food to magic.
15 plant growth forms, from tree to moss and from vine to colony, 15 plant parts, from root to spore, and 19 plant yields, from grain to poison.

name: Tooth and Claw
intro: Tooth and Claw adds time to nature. Species do not stand still: they adapt to changing conditions or die out. Predators make their prey faster, hunters make it warier, and a god's protection makes it softer. Two populations kept apart long enough become two separate species. After a great extinction, the survivors spread into every empty niche.
outcome: The living things of your universe evolve along with its history, and every epoch leaves a slightly different nature behind.

governs.title: Selection pressure
governs.text: Every species' heritable traits are kept as a living average in every region and shift with every epoch. Predator and prey, plague and host are locked in a race. A god's curse or blessing passes down a whole line.

governs.title: Niches and rivals
governs.text: A niche is made of diet, habitat, size and waking hours, and two species cannot share one for long. After great extinctions, the survivors spread into the empty niches. On islands, giants shrink and the small grow large, and abandoned domestic animals go feral.

governs.title: Energy levels
governs.text: Each level of the food chain can carry only a tenth of the life below it. Overhunt the grazers and the predators collapse. Pollinators, soil makers, dam builders and scavengers hold up whole harvests, and losing them turns into hunger and disease.

governs.title: Partners and parasites
governs.text: Pollinators feed the crops, ticks drain the herds, mistletoe strangles trees, and harmless mimics fool hunters and trackers. The yeasts and sourdough starters that every brewer, baker and monastery must keep alive are a legacy a single fire can end.

governs.title: Senses
governs.text: Night vision, smell, echolocation, vibration, heat, magnetic sense and spirit sight decide who notices whom. Peoples who see at night raid in the dark, and scent trails give spies away.

governs.title: Sleep, warmth and thorns
governs.text: Hibernating creatures vanish in their season, and a disturbed sleeper wakes hungry. Cold-blooded creatures and peoples slow down in winter and quicken in the heat. Thorns, poisons and carnivorous plants make the green itself dangerous.

governs.title: Carrion plenty
governs.text: Every war, plague, famine and massacre leaves a wave of carrion. Vultures and rats multiply, provisions spoil, disease rises, predators come closer, and the unburied dead walk as restless spirits.

depth.text: 18 heritable traits, from size to intelligence and from venom to fecundity.

depth.label: 6 food levels from producer to apex predator, and 9 keystone roles

depth.text: 6 kinds of relationship, from symbiosis to mimicry.
13 senses, from sight to spirit sight.
6 dormancy states, 5 ways of regulating body heat and 9 plant defences, from thorns to carnivory.
7 kinds of fermentation culture, from yeast to vinegar, and 9 separate fates for carrion.

name: Wyrms and Hoards
intro: Wyrms and Hoards turns monsters from specimens of a species into characters with names, histories and grudges. A dragon has a scarred body, a lair, a hoard of gold and relics, and a long memory. It sleeps, wakes when disturbed, keeps every village nearby in fear and remembers the line of whoever wounded it for generations. The ancient ones speak, bargain, sell secrets and take everything they know with them when they die.
outcome: The monsters of your universe carry as much story as its heroes.

governs.title: Named monsters
governs.text: Singular creatures with six abilities, a body that takes real wounds, and tempers from hunger to rage and from sleep to loyalty. They spread a fear that wears down the courage and prosperity of nearby settlements. The clever ones speak, bargain and make plans of their own.

governs.title: Hoards
governs.text: Raids and tribute fill the hoard, and villages can strike deals to pay it tribute. When the monster dies, the hoard becomes a treasure, and its plunder crashes luxury prices in the markets.

governs.title: Hunters and their rewards
governs.text: Quests name the monster to be hunted. A victory brings titles, dragon bone and legend. Tamed monsters carry their riders into the sky, across the sea and along the star roads, and bound ones guard temples or go to war.

governs.title: Born of the deep
governs.text: Singular horrors with bodies of crystal, fire, vapour or metal, breath of flame, frost, poison gas, snaring strands or steam, and gazes that terrify, petrify, put to sleep or drive mad. Each one hoards what it loves, flees what it hates, and wakes to deep digging or to the defiling of holy places.

governs.title: Familiar spirits
governs.text: A sorcerer binds a creature or a spirit through a rite. The familiar lends its senses, an ability or a shield against magic, and takes the backlash of a spell first. Its death wounds the sorcerer too.

governs.title: Monster contracts
governs.text: Troubled villages post bounties for coin or favours. Professional hunters study each monster's anatomy to find its weak point, and every job builds a reputation and a legend.

governs.title: The memory of the ancients
governs.text: A long-lived dragon remembers a war from three centuries ago as it happened, or as it prefers to. It teaches or sells songs, arts, rites, techniques, true names, prophecies, treasures, languages and histories. When it dies, everything it never taught dies with it.

depth.text: 12 monster tempers, from hunger to loyalty, and 11 characters, from placid to snatching.
17 body materials, from flesh to void matter.
9 habitats, among them land, water, sky, the deep and the void.
12 ways to deliver an attack and 5 attack ranges.
9 aversions, from fire to holy ground, and 8 waking triggers.
21 kinds of trophy, from meat to dragon bone.
17 kinds of knowledge the ancients can teach or sell.
13 kinds of attack effect

name: Plague Ledger
intro: Plague Ledger turns plague from a misfortune into an enemy with a name, an agent and a history. Every disease travels by its own route, targets a part of the body, spreads with caravans and armies, and hides in a host species between outbreaks. It grows resistant to treatment, changes, and comes back for those born since its last visit. Every decision made against a plague, whether closing the ports, burning the dead or praying, carries its own price.
outcome: Plagues become events that rewrite your universe's history together with its politics, faith and economy.

governs.title: Named diseases
governs.text: Every disease has a route of transmission, a lethality, an incubation period and a part of the body it targets. A disease that settles in guards its swamp: the locals are immune, while invaders die at the foot of the walls.

governs.title: Agents
governs.text: Every disease has an agent: a virus, a bacterium, a fungus, a parasite, a prion, a toxin, a nutritional deficiency, a spirit, a curse or a made agent. A treatment works only within its own class: a rite does nothing against a bacterium, and an antimicrobial does nothing against a curse. Agents evolve at their own pace, can spread through water, soil or objects, and hide in host species between outbreaks. Deficiencies spread not through contact but through famine and monotonous diets.

governs.title: Evolving plagues
governs.text: Crowded cities breed faster-spreading strains, and sparse villages breed milder ones. Every treatment used breeds resistance. Survivors stay immune, and the plague comes back for the young or changes to get past them.

governs.title: Silent carriers
governs.text: Some carriers never fall ill. A merchant, envoy or pilgrim who looks perfectly healthy starts a plague across the sea. Only a master physician who knows the theory of contagion can find them.

governs.title: True and false healers
governs.text: Disease runs through incubation, fever, crisis and then recovery or death. A healer who believes bloodletting cures fever adds to the dead, while a healer who understands contagion makes quarantine work. Addictions are diseases too.

governs.title: Where plagues come from
governs.text: Clearing forests, hunting bushmeat and herding beside wild hosts let one species' disease jump to people. Insects follow the warm seasons, and birds follow their migration routes.

governs.title: Hard choices
governs.text: Close the ports, quarantine the poor quarter, burn the dead, drive out the sick, pray or seek a cure. Each choice is paid for in trade, in revolts, in quarrels over funerals or in crowds that spread the disease.

governs.title: The race for a cure
governs.text: Hospitals, universities and monasteries race against a disease. The winner holds a cure it can sell. Inoculation trades a small risk for immunity.

depth.text: 17 routes of transmission, from the air to curses, and 17 targets, from breath to skin.
13 kinds of agent, from virus to made agent, and 14 classes of treatment, from rest to divine power.
13 ways of spreading, from caravans to sieges and from armies to mutation.
15 plague decisions, from closing the borders to seeking a cure.

depth.label: Plague decisions
values: immunise with a sample of the disease

depth.text: 27 climate leanings, from warm to dry.
3 kinds of warmth leaning
3 kinds of moisture leaning
3 kinds of altitude leaning

name: Flesh and Bone
intro: Flesh and Bone gives every living thing a real body. A mortal is no longer a pool of hit points but a body of organs, tissues, nerves and bones. An arrow can blind an eye, a sword can sever an arm, a wound can fester and kill a king. A lost limb changes an archer's life, a craftsman's work or a ruler's legitimacy.
outcome: Every wound has a story, and every scar has a meaning.

governs.title: Body plans
governs.text: Every living thing has its own body plan, from humanoid to quadruped, from winged to serpentine, from insect-like to spirit and divine forms. Each plan defines its parts, tissues and functions. Wings, venom glands, horns and tails come from a species' traits.

governs.title: Wounds
governs.text: Every wound has a part, a kind and a severity. Cuts, fractures, burns, frostbite, bites, severed limbs, curses and void touches are tracked one by one. Weapons, falls, duels, monsters, disasters and the punishments of gods all become wounds. Every death has a killing wound.

governs.title: Healing and treatment
governs.text: Wounds fester according to their kind, the disease burden and the medicine at hand. A healer diagnoses, cleans, sutures, sets bones, splints, and if need be amputates and cauterises. Lasting scars, prostheses and reattached limbs are all possible. Healers gain experience with their patients and are remembered as "saved me" or "could not heal me".

governs.title: Lasting conditions
governs.text: Chronic illness, delusions, fits of rage, melancholy, addiction, the blindness and deafness of old age, possession and void taint. A lasting condition changes what a living thing can do.

governs.title: Capacities
governs.text: How fit a body is for melee, ranged combat, command, craft, learning, presence, mobility and fertility is worked out from its wounds and conditions. Societies read bodies differently too: a scar is honour in one place and impurity in another.

governs.title: Body systems and sensitivities
governs.text: Every biology has breathing, circulation, digestion, regulation, nervous, immune, reproductive and structural systems, with tolerances for air, pressure, temperature, gravity, nutrition, sleep and poison. These tolerances decide where a creature can live unaided. Sensitivities to foods, plants, animals, substances, light, sound or power are set off on contact.

depth.text: 18 body plans, 58 body parts, 12 tissue kinds and 17 body functions.
20 damage types, from cuts to the psychic, and 30 kinds of wound.
9 wound states, from fresh to lethal, and 31 causes of harm, from battle to ceremony.
24 lasting conditions and 13 permanent maims, from losing an arm to losing one's mind.
15 medicine tiers, from herbs to reattachment, and 15 treatment steps.
12 bodily capacities, 9 body systems and 9 kinds of sensitivity.

name: Curse of the Full Moon
intro: Curse of the Full Moon gives curses, poisons, addictions, blessings and transformations a single language. Each one is an effect package, defined by how it passes from body to body, how long it lies in wait, what stages it goes through and what ends it. A werewolf's bite, a vampire's blood, a craving for drink or a god's blessing all run on the same mechanism, but each by its own rules. The night brings its own creatures, and a defiled holy place turns its curse on the one who defiled it.
outcome: Every curse in your universe has a source, a course and a cure.

governs.title: Effect packages
governs.text: Every kind of effect that settles into body and mind, from snake venom to drink and drug addiction, from lycanthropy to vampirism, from divine blessing to void taint, from possession to trauma. Every package has a route of transmission, a waiting time, stages and an end.

governs.title: Transmission
governs.text: Touch, bite, ingestion, inhalation, blood, curse, birth, rite, gaze and a lived experience. Some effects are plain to see, some can be noticed, and some stay hidden.

governs.title: Cures
governs.text: Every effect has a single cure: a rite, a technique, a medicine, time or a quest. Finding the cure can be a story in itself.

governs.title: Creatures of the night
governs.text: Werewolves who change under the full moon into a beast that still thinks. Every victim they bite can become the next hunter. Blood-hungry beings, night hunters and those who grow stronger in the dark.

governs.title: The vengeance of holy places
governs.text: Whoever robs a temple, kills in a sanctuary or defiles a grave is punished by that place's god with a curse shaped by the god's own domains. A god of the hunt sends the werewolf, and a god of blood sends the thirst.

depth.text: 20 kinds of effect package, from poison to void taint.
17 routes of transmission, from touch to experience.
4 levels of visibility, from obvious to hidden.
12 kinds of cure, from rite to quest.

depth.label: Cures
values: release by the one who laid it

depth.text: 19 kinds of curse

name: The Inner Life
intro: The Inner Life gives every mortal an inner world. A character is no longer a handful of numbers but a person with values, temperament, needs, emotions, memories, fears, dreams and life goals, and these drive every decision. A character who is betrayed remembers it, runs from what they fear, chases a dream, grieves, and at the breaking point is thrown into rage, flight, despair or revelation.
outcome: The characters of your universe live with inner worlds as coherent and deep as if an author had written them.

governs.title: Values
governs.text: Value axes from honour to tradition, from mercy to knowledge, from loyalty to family. Values come from a culture, a doctrine, a community or the person themselves. Every act is judged by these values as required, admirable, acceptable, frowned upon, shameful or unthinkable.

governs.title: Temperament and traits
governs.text: Facets of temperament from anxiety to cheerfulness and from friendliness to ambition; personality traits such as brave, craven, generous, greedy, honest and deceitful; and bodily and mental attributes from strength to intuition.

governs.title: Needs and pressures
governs.text: Bodily, social, spiritual and action needs, from sustenance to safety, from belonging to purpose, from faith to creativity. Pressures such as hunger, insecurity, crowding, poverty and humiliation weigh on whole communities.

governs.title: Emotions and mood
governs.text: Emotions from joy to pride and from fear to jealousy, moods from elation to collapse, stages of grief from shock to complicated grief, and breaking points.

governs.title: Memories and thoughts
governs.text: Memories such as "harmed me", "saved my life" and "kept their oath"; the trust, fear, respect, affection and grievance between people; and hundreds of kinds of thought, from a marriage to the death of a loved one and from a battle won to a defeat.

governs.title: Aspirations, wants and fears
governs.text: Life goals from ruling a realm to creating a masterwork, wants from marrying to taking revenge, and fears from death to the dark.

governs.title: Ideas and inspirations
governs.text: Ideas from rationalism to mysticism and from an honour code to wanderlust take root in a person or are rejected. Inspirations such as masterwork fever, research insight and heroic resolve drive a character forward.

governs.title: Dreams
governs.text: Ordinary dreams, nightmares, longings, prophetic dreams, visitations and shared dreams. Each one can be read as a sign of war, plenty, death or a journey.

depth.text: 27 value axes, 36 facets of temperament, 135 personality traits and 19 attributes.
30 needs in 5 groups and 15 kinds of social pressure.
32 emotions, 21 moods, 7 stages of grief and 9 kinds of breaking point.
43 kinds of memory, 5 parts of an opinion and 160 kinds of thought.

depth.label: Thoughts
values: felt something sent by the Creator
lived through a year of peace

depth.text: Open-ended life goals, ideas, wants, fears and dream readings.
8 kinds of inspiration and 8 kinds of dream.
3 levels of arousal

name: Cradle to Pyre
intro: Cradle to Pyre turns a mortal's life into a journey lived from birth to death. Infancy, childhood, youth, adulthood and old age are lived differently in every culture: who raises a child, what they are fed, how they are taught, at what age they start to work and at what age the law holds them responsible. Characters gain skills, choose professions and change careers, and their lives take the shape of a story: rise and fall, revenge, redemption or forbidden love.
outcome: Every character has a past and a direction.

governs.title: Infancy and childhood
governs.text: How a baby is fed and who looks after it, and the ages at which a child is weaned, named, counted as a person, put to work, held responsible by law and allowed to marry. Child labour and the protections against it.

governs.title: Socialization and education
governs.text: Every culture raises its children by example, instruction, praise, shame, punishment, ordeals, stories, play, apprenticeship, school or age sets. A school's theory of teaching, from rote to dialectic and from discovery to examination, sets how fast and how deep learning goes.

governs.title: Youth
governs.text: The years of youth, with their freedoms and duties. Youth houses, service and wandering years. Youth groups formed for sport, service, courtship, defence, faith, mischief, crime or politics.

governs.title: Skills and professions
governs.text: Skills from combat to command, from social to craft, from knowledge to survival and faith. Skills come by birth, by practice and from teachers. Professions from soldier to smith and from healer to pilot, perks that open up with talent, and careers that change with injury.

governs.title: Paths in life
governs.text: Staying in the village, joining the army, taking office, becoming an apprentice, taking vows, going into trade, taking to the road, turning bandit or studying.

governs.title: Life stories
governs.text: Story shapes such as rise and fall, rags to riches, revenge, redemption, the quest, tragedy, forbidden love, rivalry, exile and return, corruption, the fall of a house, a founding and apotheosis give a life its course.

governs.title: Death
governs.text: Causes of death from old age to battle and from childbirth to curses, and funeral customs that differ from culture to culture, from burial to sky burial and from cremation to binding the soul.

depth.text: 7 stages of life, from infancy to ancient age, and 6 ways a death can be read.
69 skills in 7 families, open-ended professions and 46 perks.
14 socialization techniques, from example to age sets, and 9 theories of education.
10 purposes for youth groups, reaching from sport to crime.
15 paths in life and 22 life story shapes.
33 causes of death and 13 funeral customs.

name: Hearts and Hands
intro: Hearts and Hands turns relationships from labels into bonds people actually live. People meet, gossip, joke, flatter, argue, flirt, propose, make up and share their secrets. Every interaction is chosen by temperament, mood, the bond itself and whether the two speak the same language, and every one leaves a mark. Passions such as love, loyalty, hatred and devotion move people to act.
outcome: The relationships in your world grow on their own out of how your characters behave.

governs.title: Relationships
governs.text: Every kind of bond, from acquaintance to closest friend, first love to spouse, rival to sworn enemy, mentor to apprentice, comrade in arms to confidant.

governs.title: Interactions
governs.text: Talking, befriending, gossiping, comforting, boasting, insulting, flirting, courting, proposing, fighting, making up, teaching, giving gifts and asking favours.

governs.title: Circles and groups
governs.text: Drinking clubs, poets' circles, hunting lodges, secret societies, study circles, prayer circles, music and craft circles. Households, courts, warbands and crews.

governs.title: Passions and persuasion
governs.text: Love, loyalty, hatred and devotion are born of a relationship, an oath, a memory or a god. People are won over by faith, self-interest, authority, evidence or fear. Persuasion can change a belief, a decision, a vote or a treaty.

governs.title: Contests
governs.text: Riddle games, insult contests, debates, games of skill, trials of wisdom, song contests and storytelling. The stake can be honour, a marriage, a wager, an office, a captive or a god's favour.

governs.title: Marriage, intimacy and birth
governs.text: Monogamy, polygamy and political marriage, and unions that end in death, divorce, annulment or war. Every culture takes its own stance on intimacy before marriage, within it, between kin or with other kinds: forbidden, frowned upon, tolerated, accepted or honoured. Vows of abstinence, pregnancy and birth, complications in labour, customs after birth and a child's legitimacy.

depth.text: 24 kinds of relationship and 28 kinds of interaction.
12 kinds of circle and 10 kinds of group.
16 passions, 8 ways to persuade and 9 aims of persuasion.
11 kinds of contest and 11 kinds of prize.
8 contexts of intimacy, each with 6 possible social stances.
9 courses a birth can take and 7 customs after birth.
6 kinds of adoption

name: Hearth and Home
intro: Hearth and Home makes everyday life part of your world. People cook, drink, bathe, share the housework, rest, have fun and spend their time the way their culture shapes it. Every people has its own cuisine, its own taverns, its own idea of clean and its own habits of leisure.
outcome: Between the great events, ordinary life is part of the world too, and it gives any writer who needs a scene a setting ready to use.

governs.title: Households
governs.text: Who belongs to a household, their roles and how they make a living. Who carries the housework and how heavy it is: food, water, fuel, cleaning, textiles, care of children and elders, animals and repairs. Servants who work for wages, for board and lodging, or bound.

governs.title: Kitchen and meals
governs.text: Ways of cooking, from raw and boiled to fried and fermented. Kinds of meal, from everyday dishes to feast tables, rite meals, rations and healing food. How every people eats: from plant eaters to blood drinkers, from stone eaters to those who feed on light.

governs.title: Taverns and intoxicants
governs.text: Beer, wine, spirits, incense, leaf, fungus and essences. Each can belong to daily life, feasts, rites or mourning, or be forbidden. Taverns are where talk, gossip and intrigue meet.

governs.title: How time is shared
governs.text: For every culture, class and stage of life, how time divides between work, housework, care, rest, sleep, worship, learning, leisure, travel and service. Beings who never sleep or eat have their place in the count too.

governs.title: Grooming and cleanliness
governs.text: How often and where people wash (at home, in a bathhouse, in a river or as a rite), care of hair and body, scents, ideas of cleanliness and the handling of waste.

governs.title: Leisure
governs.text: Conversation, games, sport, music, crafts, collecting, reading, outings, tourism, drinking, extra worship, rest and media.

governs.title: Space and touch
governs.text: Each culture's rules on personal distance, touch, sitting and posture. Etiquette and diplomacy read them.

depth.text: 13 kinds of housework.
35 ways of cooking, from raw to synthesised, and 9 kinds of meal.
16 diets among peoples.
11 intoxicants and 9 ways of using them.
14 shares of time and 19 kinds of pastime.

name: Strange Flesh
intro: Strange Flesh takes the peoples of your world beyond the human mould. A people can be incorporeal, aquatic, winged, subterranean, hive-minded, plant-like, constructed, ageless, shapeshifting, gaseous, crystalline or deathless. These differences are not decoration: they decide where a people can live, what it eats, how it fights, how it is born and dies, and how it deals with other peoples.
outcome: The peoples of your world live with every consequence of being truly different.

governs.title: Biological variants
governs.text: Each people's body follows the rules of its variant. Spirit beings do not eat, yet they are not beyond touch either. Aquatic peoples struggle on land. Hive minds act as a single will. Ageless peoples grow and shrink at a pace of their own. The deathless need a different economy and a different faith.

governs.title: Innate traits
governs.text: Dark sight, cold blood, wings, life on land and in water, thick hide, keen senses, venom, regeneration, burrowing and the hive mind.

governs.title: Diets of peoples
governs.text: From plant eaters to meat eaters, fish eaters to scavengers, blood drinkers to stone eaters, essence feeders to light feeders. How a people eats shapes its farming, its trade and its wars directly.

governs.title: Dealing with other peoples
governs.text: Peoples with different bodies share the same land, the same market and the same battlefield on different terms. These differences steer alliances, trade and conflict.

depth.text: 19 biological variants, from incorporeal to undead.
Open-ended innate traits, from dark sight to the hive mind.
16 diets among peoples, reaching as far as feeding on light.
10 core innate traits

name: Codes of Honour
intro: Codes of Honour gives every culture a morality. What is required, what is admirable, what is shameful and what is unthinkable changes from culture to culture. For one people honour comes before everything; for another it is dignity, or face. Reputations are built on heroism, generosity, wisdom or cruelty. The gap between word and deed is recorded too: anyone who champions a value and does the opposite may one day see that hypocrisy come to light.
outcome: Your characters and peoples make their choices out of their own sense of right and wrong.

governs.title: Honour models
governs.text: Every culture reads a person's worth through one of three models: inner dignity, honour in the eyes of others, or face within the community.

governs.title: Moral stances
governs.text: Every act, from execution to mutilation, betrayal to mercy for an enemy, human sacrifice to temple building, book burning to duelling, counts in each culture as required, admirable, acceptable, frowned upon, shameful or unthinkable.

governs.title: Reputation
governs.text: Renown for heroism, honour, cruelty, piety, generosity, wisdom, cunning or skill, or a name as a troublemaker. Reputation builds up and is spent as prestige, piety, dread and tyranny.

governs.title: Shame and punishment
governs.text: Public shaming, stripping of titles, forced confession, fines, flogging, exile and branding. Punishments work through reputation as far as the culture's honour model allows. Shame left unmended turns into a grudge within a household.

governs.title: Word and deed
governs.text: The values and beliefs a person champions are weighed against the deeds recorded against them. The gap, and who knows about it, is recorded. When hypocrisy comes to light, a reputation collapses.

depth.text: 4 honour models and 6 degrees of moral stance.
66 kinds of act weighed by moral codes.
13 axes of reputation and 6 currencies of reputation.
34 kinds of punishment, from fines to forced dormancy.

name: Ties of Blood
intro: Ties of Blood gives every mortal a lineage and a genetic inheritance. Children take after their parents: height, build, skin, hair and eye colour, face and voice pass down by the rules of heredity. Long life, fertility, resistance to disease and magical gifts are carried in the blood too. Lineages are bound by kinship: who is whose heir, who may marry whom, and what an aunt, an uncle or a godparent owes.
outcome: Houses, dynasties and clans live as real bloodlines you can trace across the generations.

governs.title: Genetics
governs.text: Every mortal has a genome. Looks and leanings pass from generation to generation through dominant and recessive genes, and they mutate. Marriage between close kin raises the risks. A child's talents come from the potential inherited from its parents combined with how it is raised. A house's telltale features are carried in its genes.

governs.title: Appearance
governs.text: Genes, scars, lost limbs and curse marks shape how a character looks. Beauty is judged by each people's own taste. Rare features make a person recognisable, and children resemble their parents to a measurable degree.

governs.title: Magical gifts
governs.text: Each form of magic has its own gift genes: dormant, recessive, or rare and wild. The share of the gifted within a people depends on how that people treats them: an honoured gift spreads, a persecuted gift dwindles. Mage orders test the children.

governs.title: Kinship
governs.text: Descent reckoned through one line, through the other, through both sides, through both lines at once or by choice. Marriage customs from monogamy to group marriage. Inheritance to the firstborn, to the lastborn, through the second line, by election or by merit.

governs.title: Kin roles and duties
governs.text: Parent, child, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, the siblings of parents, cousins, in-laws, co-spouse, chosen kin, godparent and blood sibling. Every culture gives each role its own duties.

governs.title: Kin groups
governs.text: Lineages, clans, phratries, moieties, kindreds and houses. Every group has its rule of membership, shared holdings (land, titles, temples), a head, a council and rules for marrying out.

governs.title: Households and dwellings
governs.text: Kinds of dwelling, from hut to palace, tent to tower, ship to apartment, and the shape of the household.

depth.text: 60 gene loci for looks and leanings.
5 ways of reckoning descent, open-ended marriage customs and 9 inheritance customs.
21 kin roles and 9 forms of kin group.
11 household forms and 18 kinds of dwelling.
6 kinship naming systems

name: The Teeming Millions
intro: The Teeming Millions turns a people's population from a single number into a living society. Every community counts its children, adults and elders by class and condition: maimed, veteran, sick, enslaved or captive. Births rise and fall with food and stress, famines take the youngest and the oldest, and wars take the young who fight them. When someone stands out from the crowd, a famine orphan, say, or the first victim of a plague, they gain a name, a memory and a life.
outcome: The peoples of your world live as one unbroken whole, from nameless crowds to named individuals.

governs.title: Population cohorts
governs.text: Every community counts its cohorts by age, class and condition. Births, deaths, migration and war losses all play out in these cohorts.

governs.title: From crowd to person
governs.text: When something notable happens in a crowd, one person steps out of it and becomes a named character. No one with a name ever melts back into the crowd. Characters nothing touches are put to sleep and wake when something reaches them.

governs.title: Division of labour
governs.text: Farming, herding, fishing, mining, crafts, trade, soldiering, the clergy, scholarship, building, service and idleness. Communities divide their labour by need, price and law.

governs.title: Social mobility
governs.text: Ennoblement, enslavement, freedom and ruin. A mortal can change class.

governs.title: Generations
governs.text: Every generation is shaped by what it lived through in its youth: a great war, a victory, a defeat, a plague, a famine, a golden age or a conquest. When it comes of age it shifts values, when it gives way it brings unrest, and it hands part of its legacy to the next.

governs.title: Population policy
governs.text: Realms, faiths, peoples, companies and gods can set out to grow a population, hold it steady, shrink it, shift its balance of age or class, open land to settlement or empty it. Their tools are birth rewards and birth taxes, marriage laws, child limits and child support, inheritance rules, settlement grants, migration permits and bans, expulsions, resettlements, health campaigns and the teachings of faith.

depth.text: 6 age groups, open-ended social classes and 10 cohort conditions.
19 lines of work.
9 social mobility events.
19 kinds of event that shape generations.
10 aims of population policy and 17 tools to reach them.
4 reproductive roles

name: Many Banners
intro: Many Banners turns who people are from a single label into a layered identity. A person belongs at once to a people, a faith, a class, a hometown, a house, a profession, a generation, a realm and a circle. Which identity comes to the fore depends on the moment: a holy war brings faith forward, a year of famine brings class, an enemy army on the land brings people and realm. Peoples under foreign rule rise to bring back their old ways.
outcome: Your societies split and unite on their own, out of the identities of the people in them.

governs.title: Layers of identity
governs.text: Every city, people and named mortal carries identity in 14 layers. For each identity, its value, how tightly it is held and how much it matters are recorded.

governs.title: Identity to the fore
governs.text: Holy wars, famines, invasions, strikes, sermons, segregated quarters and gods bring certain identities forward. Marriages and guilds that cross peoples and faiths soften those lines. Over time, identities settle back into balance.

governs.title: Revivals
governs.text: Peoples under foreign rule pass through 6 stages. Then comes a new stability, or the movement is crushed. Peoples turn to bringing back the old ways, rallying round a prophet who joins old and new, or taking on the conqueror's culture whole.

governs.title: Popular movements
governs.text: Movements for abolition, independence, revival, land reform, the vote and peace. Movements can fight to revive a language, bring back an old god or drive out foreigners.

depth.text: 14 layers of identity, from people to circle, and 15 drivers that bring an identity forward.
6 stages, 6 ways and 6 aims of revival.
14 kinds of popular movement.

name: Fire in the Streets
intro: Fire in the Streets models crowds as the sum of their people. Every crowd is made of individuals, each with a breaking point of their own. The price of bread doubles, a few apprentices throw stones and nobody stops them. Their nerve eases the dockworkers' fear, their anger stirs the loom workers, and by evening a district is burning. A crowd can turn into a riot, a panic, a lynching, a mass conversion, a revolt, a strike, a procession or a religious revival.
outcome: A city's fate hangs on who moves first, and every time it plays out for reasons of its own.

governs.title: The mood of the crowd
governs.text: Every district's anger, fear and fervour are tracked separately. Quarantines, laws, uprisings by other groups, executions, fires, raids and miracles stir the crowd.

governs.title: Chain reactions
governs.text: Every person has a threshold of their own. Anger, fear, fervour and the urge to go along lower it; deterrence raises it. Once one threshold is crossed, the next is easier to cross, and the event snowballs.

governs.title: Crowd actions
governs.text: Riot, panic, lynching, mass conversion, revolt, strike, procession and religious revival. The target, course and end of each are recorded.

governs.title: From crowd to movement
governs.text: A crowd's anger can harden into a lasting popular movement. Movements organise, raise leaders and can last for years.

depth.text: 15 kinds of crowd action, from riot to religious revival.
7 crowd feelings, tracked separately in every district
19 kinds of crowd trigger.

name: Feast and Funeral
intro: Feast and Funeral fills a people's calendar and life cycle with ceremony. Festivals, fasts, funerals, coming-of-age rites, weddings, taboos, offerings, pilgrimages and laws of hospitality each play out with a real effect, a season and a cost. People mark their bodies, change their names and move up through age grades. They come together at weddings, funerals, coronations and tournaments. At these gatherings love affairs begin, secrets come out, plots are hatched, and sometimes blood is spilled despite the law of hospitality.
outcome: Every people has a rhythm of life of its own, and the most important scenes play out at these ceremonies.

governs.title: Customs
governs.text: Festivals, fasts, funeral rites, coming-of-age rites, wedding rites, taboos, offerings, pilgrimages, laws of hospitality, duelling customs, mourning and harvest rites. Each has its season, a cost in grain or incense, and a real effect on unity, contentment, piety, fertility or safety.

governs.title: Gatherings
governs.text: Feasts, weddings, funerals, coronations, tournaments, hunts, pilgrimages, councils, summits, festivals, fairs, performances, trials, executions and processions. Who attends depends on bonds, obligation, distance and invitation. The law of hospitality, and the morality that forbids killing a guest, hold violence in check.

governs.title: Body marking
governs.text: Tattoos, scars, piercings, shaping, filed teeth, cosmetics, jewellery and brands. Each mark can stand for status, clan, a deed, an age set, marriage, mourning, protection or a crime.

governs.title: Naming
governs.text: A given name, a parent's name, a clan name, or a parent known by their child's name. Birth names, secret names, deed names, initiation names, marriage names, vow names and ascension names.

governs.title: Age grades
governs.text: Children, youths, warriors, junior elders and senior elders. Every passage is marked by a rite.

governs.title: Death work and funerals
governs.text: Those who wash the dead, prepare them, keep the remains, lead the rites, mourn, keep the records and carry the dead. In every culture these roles are honoured or shunned, and each has its pay and its guild. Remains are buried, burned, exposed, preserved, given to the water or kept. Every method has a cost, a place and an effect on health.

8 kinds of rite of passage.

name: The Gift
intro: The Gift brings a gift economy to your world. A gift is never free: every gift creates a debt, and that debt must be repaid, refused or returned with more. Gifts seal alliances, complete weddings, feed the hungry and set the terms between gods and mortals. Ceremonial gift circuits passing between peoples keep the roads safe.
outcome: The bonds in your world are made not only by treaties but by who owes what to whom.

governs.title: The gift ledger
governs.text: Who gave what to whom, when and on what occasion. Every gift stands open, returned, refused, destroyed or lapsed. Gifts left unanswered wear away a reputation.

governs.title: Occasions
governs.text: Courtesy, feasts, ceremonial circuits, offerings, marriage, return gifts, alliance and relief.

governs.title: Ceremonial circuits
governs.text: Gifts that pass between peoples in a set order. Lands the circuit crosses are closed to outlaws. Killing a guest who comes with the circuit is among the gravest disgraces.

governs.title: Debts to the gods
governs.text: A god's standing among a people is read from the ledger of offerings. Gods give gifts too, and their gifts create a debt as well.

governs.title: Hospitality
governs.text: The law of hospitality sets out what host and guest owe each other, and whoever breaks it pays a heavy price.

depth.text: 16 occasions for giving.

name: Muse and Market
intro: Muse and Market puts art and sport at the heart of a people's life. Songs, epics, plays, statues, frescoes, carpets, mosaics, books, dances and architectural ornament are made as real works that are shown, sold, copied and handed down. Art movements are born, spread and give way to new ones. Collectors, dealers, patrons and connoisseurs build an art market. Teams, clubs and leagues fill the stadiums.
outcome: Every people has a culture of its own, with masterpieces of its own.

governs.title: Works of art
governs.text: Works from songs to epics, plays to statues, frescoes to mosaics, books to architectural ornament. Each has a maker, a subject, a quality and a value. Masterpieces raise a city's prestige and draw travellers.

governs.title: Arts and movements
governs.text: Music, poetry, dance, theatre, painting, sculpture, architectural style, textile art and calligraphy. Art movements are born, spread, challenge the established ones and fade.

governs.title: The art market
governs.text: Collectors, dealers, patrons and connoisseurs. Works are bought and sold, and their prices shift. Fake works, fake relics, fake documents and fake brands slip into the market and can be exposed.

governs.title: Cultural rights
governs.text: Rights over songs, dances, stories, rites, designs, names, titles, brands and market privileges. Rights are created, inherited, bought, licensed, stolen or granted.

governs.title: Sport
governs.text: Team games, races, combat sports and athletics. Clubs and leagues compete across seasons and crown champions. Every sport, from ball games to trials of strength, has heroes of its own.

depth.text: 19 art forms, from song to architectural ornament.
9 roles in the art market and 8 kinds of forgery.
13 kinds of cultural right and 9 ways to gain one.

name: Blues and Greens
intro: Blues and Greens turns sport from entertainment into a seat of power. Clubs compete across seasons, crown champions and split the city's heart between them. When support spreads across districts, classes and faiths, a club becomes a political faction. If a disputed race is lost on the same day a new tax is announced, the stands empty into the streets.
outcome: A story that starts on a racetrack can burn down a capital.

governs.title: Clubs and leagues
governs.text: Team games, races, combat sports and athletics. Clubs compete in arenas and at festivals, season after season, in leagues of rival clubs. Every sport has its own champions.

governs.title: Supporters
governs.text: Each club's share of support in the city is counted cohort by cohort and district by district.

governs.title: Betting
governs.text: Wagers on every race raise or sink households' fortunes. A lucky season makes a family rich; a bad one drowns it in debt.

governs.title: Hippodrome factions
governs.text: When a club's colours line up with a class, a district or a faith, the club becomes a political faction with real sway over public opinion. Rulers can buy a club, and with it the voice of the stands.

governs.title: Riots in the stands
governs.text: A club's crowd is a riot waiting for its spark. A lost championship can set off a chain of uprisings across the city.

depth.text: 8 kinds of club, from team games to athletics, 66 kinds of judged act and 74 kinds of crime.
Support is tracked by cohort and by district.
A lost match is one of 19 triggers that can start a riot in the city.

name: Tongues of Ages
intro: Tongues of Ages gives every people a real language and changes it along with history. Languages evolve through ordered sound laws: through contact, prestige, migration or on their own. A language splits into dialects, sister languages are born, and place names keep the language's older forms. Dead scripts are cracked with bilingual stones and patient scholars. Every treaty, every sermon and every order has to cross the line of mutual understanding.
outcome: Every name in your world carries a meaning, and every word has a history.

governs.title: Structure of language
governs.text: Every language has a word order, a morphology and a number system. A language can be carried by sound, sign, scent, colour, telepathy, data or chemistry.

governs.title: Sound change
governs.text: Every language builds up ordered sound laws made of shifts, lenitions, vowel shifts, mergers and losses. These laws apply at the start of a word, at the end, between vowels or everywhere. Contact, prestige, migration, drift or a decree can set them off. Sister languages part ways, and scholars can reconstruct the parent tongue.

governs.title: Meaning change
governs.text: Word meanings broaden, narrow, worsen, improve, turn euphemistic or return to an older sense. Words can be everyday, sacred, poetic or archaic.

governs.title: Scripts
governs.text: Writing systems are invented, reformed, simplified and borrowed. Writing materials from clay tablets to paper, from metal plates to knotted cords.

governs.title: Cracking dead scripts
governs.text: Bilingual stones, living sister languages and patient scholars decipher lost scripts over the seasons. Partial readings give partial knowledge, and mistranslations live on as theories and legends.

governs.title: Barriers and bridges
governs.text: Every treaty, sale, sermon and battle order has to pass through understanding. Interpreters close the gap, common tongues spread along trade routes, and mixed languages grow into creoles. Sign languages arise among the deaf, those under vows of silence, silent hunters and those whose tongues were cut. Classes, castes, guilds, courts, thieves and sailors develop their own ways of speaking.

governs.title: Languages of power
governs.text: A conquered people with a great literature can conquer its conquerors. Realms make languages official, make them liturgical, ban them or revive them. Every god has a sacred language whose words are rites.

name: The Rewritten Past
intro: The Rewritten Past turns history itself into a matter of dispute. An event happens once but is told in countless ways. A new dynasty's official chronicle makes its founder the child of a god, the valley's folk songs remember a stable hand who poisoned their master, and the record of a merchant from across the sea says both are wrong.
outcome: Your world's history is not one true account but many competing ones, and that competition makes stories of its own.

governs.title: Accounts
governs.text: Official chronicles, folk memory, foreign records, scripture, epics, inscriptions, founding myths and the memory of elders. Each account tells the same event from its own point of view.

governs.title: The stance of an account
governs.text: An account can glorify an event, vilify it, ignore it or report it plainly. Which account spreads depends on who wrote it and how it travels.

governs.title: Media of accounts
governs.text: Artworks, books, oral tradition and inscriptions. Each medium lasts differently and spreads in its own way.

governs.title: Calendars and dating
governs.text: Keeping dates by regnal years, from a founding, by religious events or by cycles of the sky.

governs.title: Rewriting the past
governs.text: Regimes rewrite history in their own favour, burn books and erase inscriptions. Suppressed accounts live on in folk memory and can surface again one day.

8 stances an account can take, from glorifying to ignoring.

name: Forge and Furnace
intro: Forge and Furnace builds a real production chain into your world's economy. Every item is made from a material, every material is taken from somewhere, and all production happens with a method, a source of energy and a level of quality. Industry follows geography: rivers give water power, winds turn mills, and magic and divine power are sources of energy too. Production leaves pollution behind, and mines and workshops bring profit to their owners and danger to their workers.
outcome: You can trace whose hands made a sword, a ship or a temple, from what material and at what cost.

governs.title: Materials
governs.text: Materials from wood to bone, copper to steel, gold to dragon bone. They fall into organic, stone, metal, precious and exotic. Some come from a god's remains, a dead star, a beast or leak crystals. Every material has a hardness, a value and its uses: body, weapon, armour, hull or fabric.

governs.title: Goods
governs.text: Goods from grain to livestock, timber to fuel, weapons to luxuries. They fall into subsistence, industrial, strategic and luxury goods.

governs.title: Extraction
governs.text: Mining, quarrying, logging, fishing, herding, farming and gathering. Each has its own dangers: cave-ins, flooding, felling accidents, drowning and goring.

governs.title: Workshops and methods
governs.text: Workshops from mill to foundry, tannery to shipyard. Methods for every process, from harvesting by hand to deep-sea fleets, from axe felling to the water-powered sawmill. Geography decides where industry is born.

governs.title: Energy
governs.text: Muscle, water, wind, heat, magic and divine power. On frozen worlds heat means survival, and a fuel shortage means communities freeze to death.

governs.title: Quality
governs.text: Quality tiers from poor to masterwork and legendary artifact. Master crafters win renown.

governs.title: Pollution
governs.text: Production fouls the air, the water and the soil. Pollution harms health and harvests.

governs.title: Ownership and profit
governs.text: Workshops and mines belong to guilds, merchants, cults, the realm, a house or a community. Every workshop keeps a ledger: sales, inputs, wages, upkeep and taxes.

governs.title: Chemistry
governs.text: Dyes, soaps, mordants, tanning agents, fertilisers, medicines, incendiaries and explosives.

name: Coin of the Realm
intro: Coin of the Realm builds a working money economy into your world. Markets set prices by supply and demand, realms mint coin, merchants extend credit and insurers take on risk. Famine drives prices up, war cuts off trade, and hoarders corner markets. One realm's money gains or loses value against another's.
outcome: Your world's economic crises, fortunes and bankruptcies arise from the logic of a real economy.

governs.title: Markets and prices
governs.text: In every market, the price of every good moves with supply and demand, the season and trade. Shortages and gluts show in prices at once.

governs.title: Money
governs.text: Realms mint money. Its value rests on the realm's strength and trustworthiness. Exchange rates shift between realms.

governs.title: Credit and debt
governs.text: Loans are made, repaid, defaulted on or forgiven. A realm's credit can be normal, strained, in default or under restructuring.

governs.title: Savings
governs.text: Households and institutions put wealth aside. Savings can turn into investment.

governs.title: Insurance
governs.text: Cargo, house and life insurance. Insurers take on risk, and one great disaster can ruin them.

governs.title: Speculation
governs.text: Hoarders stockpile goods, then sell or go bust. Cornering a market or dumping goods onto it changes prices drastically.

governs.title: Trade policy
governs.text: Tariffs, subsidies and embargoes.

name: The Salt Road
intro: The Salt Road turns trade into living routes across the map. Goods travel by road, river, sea, caravan and sky. Every route opens, falls under blockade, closes or decays. Bandits, seas, beasts and weather can stop a caravan in its tracks. Along the trade routes, trading posts are founded, cities grow rich, and travellers and pilgrims come and go.
outcome: Your world's economies and cultures are joined along the paths these routes follow.

governs.title: Trade routes
governs.text: Road, river, sea, caravan and sky routes. Every route forms, opens, falls under blockade, closes or decays from neglect.

governs.title: Losses
governs.text: Bandits, the sea, beasts and the weather take their cut of trade. Keeping the road safe is a realm's duty.

governs.title: Caravans and carriers
governs.text: Carts, pack animals, porters, barges, ships and sky barges. Caravans load, set out, run late, arrive, are raided or vanish.

governs.title: Cargo and preservation
governs.text: Perishables, livestock, bulk cargo and fine goods. Cargo is kept by salting, ice or magic. Containers from amphorae to chests.

governs.title: Trading posts
governs.text: Trading posts founded in distant lands change the local economy and culture.

governs.title: Travel and tourism
governs.text: Travellers and pilgrims use the trade routes and carry money and news to the cities they visit.

governs.title: Vertical integration
governs.text: A merchant house can control the whole chain, from mine to workshop and from workshop to market.

governs.title: Navigation aids
governs.text: Compass, astrolabe, log line and charts make sea routes safe.

name: Yoke and Wage
intro: Yoke and Wage brings the price and shape of labour into your world. People find work or lose it, and their wages rise or fall. Some work freely; others are bound to corvée, serfdom or slavery. When basic needs go unmet, hunger, cold, sickness and unrest follow. Unpaid wages can send a whole city into the streets.
outcome: Your world's social conflicts arise from who does the work and who reaps the reward.

governs.title: Work and wages
governs.text: Lines of work from farming to service, each with its wage. Wages move with the supply of labour, prices and the law. Unemployment wears down a community's prosperity and peace.

governs.title: Division of labour
governs.text: People choose their work by class, prices, buildings and resources. Corvée and held labour limit that choice.

governs.title: Tiers of need
governs.text: Hunger, loss of herds, cold, sickness, impiety, loss of status, heavy toil, insecurity and magical want. Every unmet need puts a community under strain.

governs.title: Bound labour
governs.text: Serfs and slaves, corvée and debt bondage. The bound can win their freedom, and the free can be enslaved.

governs.title: Strikes and unpaid wages
governs.text: Unpaid wages stir up crowds, and strikes bring workshops to a halt.

governs.title: Social classes
governs.text: Classes from farmer to noble, from priest to the idle, and movement between them.
