name: Walls and Wards
intro: Walls and Wards turns cities from single points on the map into settlements that live street by street. As a hamlet grows into a village, a village into a town and a town into a city, new districts open: markets, craft quarters, temple quarters, harbours, citadels, palaces and slums. Rents sort the classes street by street; places that services reach thrive, and places they miss decay. Cities that prepare for disaster stay standing; those that do not fall and are rebuilt.
outcome: Your world's cities are real places that shape the lives of the people who live in them.

governs.title: Districts and zones
governs.text: Districts from farmland to markets, craft quarters to temple quarters, harbours to citadels, slums to palaces, foreign quarters to cemeteries. New kinds of district open as the city grows. Zones for government, housing, commerce, industry, farming, civic life and green space.

governs.title: Rents and the displaced
governs.text: Temples, fountains and parks raise land values; tanneries, prisons, crime and dark memories lower them. Rents sort the classes street by street, and rising values push the poor out.

governs.title: Services
governs.text: Water, faith, the watch, healing, markets, schools, baths and fire brigades. Each service covers the streets around it. Beyond its reach come thirst, crime, disease, impiety and ignorance. Public services such as education, health, sport, culture and social welfare.

governs.title: Housing
governs.text: When services and goods arrive, shacks become huts, then houses, mansions and manors; when they leave, homes fall into ruin. When migrants arrive faster than housing, slums spread and feed plague, crime and fire.

governs.title: City form
governs.text: A city grows organically, by plan, in rings of walls, on a grid, upward or by sprawling. Its form decides how fire spreads, how goods move and whether the inner walls hold.

governs.title: Charitable institutions
governs.text: Poorhouses, orphanages, foundling homes, leper houses and widows' houses take in the maimed and the abandoned, and their patrons earn merit. Granaries, alms, almshouses and neighbourhood relief.

governs.title: Disaster preparedness and rebuilding
governs.text: Levees, firebreaks, seawalls, drills, stockpiles and watchtowers keep a disaster from turning into ruin. Aid in goods, healers and labour sent by rival realms leaves a debt of gratitude. After fire, flood, earthquake, storm or sack, the city is rebuilt by plan or by opportunity.

name: Wonders Rising
intro: Wonders Rising turns buildings from decoration into working parts of the universe. Every temple, library, observatory, citadel, bank, shipyard, aqueduct and arena does a real job and needs staff to run it. When plague kills the scribes, the library still stands but its knowledge sleeps. Realms race for wonders: the first to finish wins, and envy follows the losers. At cosmic scale, star cages, orbital rings and engines that move whole worlds are built too.
outcome: Raising, razing or abandoning a building is an event that changes the history of your universe.

governs.title: Buildings and what they do
governs.text: From temples to libraries, citadels to banks, aqueducts to tombs, every building has a real function. Granaries feed sieges, hospitals slow epidemics, and observatories predict eclipses.

governs.title: Labour and upkeep
governs.text: Every building needs staff and upkeep. As its condition falls, so does its function. Buildings are planned, built, completed, damaged and ruined.

governs.title: Sections and forms
governs.text: The sections of a building, from foundation to walls, gatehouse to dome, hall to tower. Building forms, from halls and pyramids to domes and bridges.

governs.title: Building materials
governs.text: Materials from mud brick to hydraulic concrete, each with its own strength, weathering, and resistance to fire and water.

governs.title: The wonder race
governs.text: Wonders and cosmic works are unique to a world or to the whole cosmos. Several realms build at once, and the first to finish wins. A wonder feeds its city's prestige and draws travellers from every coast. The loser salvages some of the stone, and the half-built ruin fills with legends.

governs.title: Megastructures
governs.text: Star cages that harvest a sun's essence and dim it, orbital rings, world-bridges, void lighthouses for safe passage, and planetary engines that push a world out of its orbit.

governs.title: Museums, collections and gardens
governs.text: Royal collections, temple treasuries and museums draw scholars and tourists, become loot in every sack and come home as a clause of peace. Physic gardens supply healers, hunting parks shelter game, and sacred groves and cemeteries serve their own purposes.

governs.title: Lifting water
governs.text: Shadufs, waterwheels, Archimedes screws, chain pumps and steam pumps raise water to the terraces and drain the deep mines.

name: Heirlooms and Relics
intro: Heirlooms and Relics gives objects a past. Every crafted work carries its maker's mark and a history of its owners and the events it saw: killings, battles, coronations, thefts and burials. An item's fame grows with each event, and an item famous enough becomes a legend in its own right. Crowns carry legitimacy, the bones of saints draw pilgrims, and cursed swords corrupt their bearers.
outcome: The objects of your universe carry as many stories as its characters, and chasing an item becomes an adventure of its own.

governs.title: Provenance
governs.text: Every item has a maker's mark and a history of its owners and the events it lived through. Fame builds with every event.

governs.title: Decorations
governs.text: Studded, inlaid, carved, rune-marked or menacingly spiked decorations. Carved images tell of real events and keep that event alive in the culture.

governs.title: Works of obsession
governs.text: Works born when a crafter is seized by a fever to create, each with a unique name, the highest quality and often an enchantment. Greedy nobles want them, and thieves go after them.

governs.title: Regalia
governs.text: Crowns, sceptres, seals, rings and banners. Whoever holds the regalia holds legitimacy. Usurpers go after the crown, and losing it is a humiliation the whole realm feels.

governs.title: Relics and curses
governs.text: The bones of saints and fragments of dead gods sometimes heal, draw pilgrims and invite relic raids. Cursed swords breed bloodthirst, betrayal, wasting, madness or misfortune in their bearers. A relic left by an ancient civilisation may keep working, fail or fall dormant. Peoples may treat it as sacred, use it as a tool, forbid it or display it as heritage.

governs.title: Lenses and clocks
governs.text: Spectacles restore sight lost to age and lengthen scholars' careers, and telescopes predict eclipses. Public clocks order labour, synchronise armies and let ships fix their position.

governs.title: Locks, vaults and decaying archives
governs.text: Thieves test their skill against locksmiths, seals and guards. Papyrus rots in damp ground and clay tablets bake hard in a fire, so the material decides what history remembers.

8 kinds of lock, 16 writing media and 12 kinds of container.

name: Underworld
intro: Underworld organises the dark side of the city. Crime families, thieves' guilds, smuggling rings and pirate brotherhoods carve up the city district by district, each with its own ranks and treasury. Bribes buy the watch, and hooks made of secrets and debts buy the judges. A vow of silence holds the family together: an informer fears the family more than the gallows.
outcome: The cities of your universe carry a shadow order with its own rules, wars and heroes.

governs.title: Criminal organisations
governs.text: Crime families, thieves' guilds, smuggling rings and pirate brotherhoods. Each has its own ladder of ranks and its own treasury.

governs.title: Rackets and their takings
governs.text: Protection, smuggling, gambling, fencing, kidnapping and counterfeiting. Each brings its own income and its own victims.

governs.title: Turf wars
governs.text: Families hold the city district by district. When they fight over a street, the maimings, murders and collapsing order touch everyone who lives there.

governs.title: Officials on the payroll
governs.text: Bribes buy the watch, and hooks made of secrets and debts buy the judges.

governs.title: The law of silence
governs.text: Membership is sealed with an oath, and the family punishes its traitors.

governs.title: Crush or co-opt
governs.text: Realms can try to crush the families with thief-takers, watchmen and purges, or turn them into informers and license pirates as privateers.

governs.title: Outlaws and bounties
governs.text: An outlaw loses the protection of the law, and robbing or killing one is no crime. Bounties draw hunters. An outlaw who spares the poor can become their folk hero. Temples, hospitality and the right of asylum can give fugitives sanctuary.

depth.text: 8 kinds of criminal organisation, each with 4 ranks: leader, officer, member and novice.
15 kinds of racket.
5 stances a state can take towards crime.
8 kinds of fugitive, such as outlaws, the accused and defectors, and 8 kinds of sanctuary.

name: Throne and Council
intro: Throne and Council turns realms into governed states. Every realm has a form of government, offices, laws, taxes and a council. Councillors improve relations, train troops, collect taxes, break up schemes, convert provinces or fight corruption. Taxes bring in revenue but also stir unrest. Provinces try to break away from the centre, and the court lives on its own intrigues.
outcome: The politics of your universe grow out of working institutions and the decisions of the people who fill them.

governs.title: Forms of government
governs.text: Forms of government from chiefdom to monarchy, theocracy to oligarchy, republic to empire, hive council to god realm, junta to corporate state.

governs.title: Offices
governs.text: Ruler, heir, regent, chancellor, marshal, treasurer, high judge, spymaster, governor, ambassador, herald, chaplain, court scholar, head of state and of government, minister, general, admiral and speaker. Each office carries its own powers: rule, succession, negotiation, command, treasury, justice, espionage, governing, embassy, proclamation, preaching, research and jest.

governs.title: Council tasks
governs.text: Improve relations, train troops, collect taxes, disrupt schemes, convert a province and purge corruption.

governs.title: Laws
governs.text: Laws from the rule of succession to the division of inheritance, from land tenure to slavery, from the tax rate to the levy.

governs.title: Taxes and mandates
governs.text: Land, poll, trade and consumption taxes and the tithe. Mandates for production, export bans, building, famine relief, curfews, slum clearance, preparation and enclosure.

governs.title: Subject states
governs.text: Vassals, tributaries, marches, personal unions, client states, colonies and protectorates. In a crisis, demands such as ceding land, releasing a vassal, converting or paying up.

governs.title: The court
governs.text: Court positions such as steward, champion, physician, tutor, chronicler and master of revels.

governs.title: Separatism and constitutions
governs.text: Provinces can try to break away from the centre. Constitutions limit powers and can be rewritten.

name: Patrons and Puppets
intro: Patrons and Puppets runs the unseen rules of power. Every realm knows who chose its ruler and whose backing keeps the ruler standing: small circles are bought with gifts and offices, large ones with roads and granaries. Legitimacy rests on tradition, charisma or law, and each one fails in its own way. Where institutions are weak, the bonds between patrons and clients do the work. Governors and generals gather power, and rulers try to keep them in balance.
outcome: The political crises of your universe grow out of the real balance of power.

governs.title: The winning coalition
governs.text: Who chooses the ruler: the tribe, the nobles, a council, the army, the priests, the citizens, a party, the shareholders or an algorithm. Small circles are satisfied with private rewards, large ones with public goods.

governs.title: Legitimacy
governs.text: Traditional legitimacy weakens when the succession breaks, charismatic legitimacy with defeat and death, and legal legitimacy with corruption. When a charismatic founder dies, the realm must turn that authority into institutions.

governs.title: Patrons and clients
governs.text: Favours and protection bind households, retainers, officials and commanders to the powerful. Offices are sold, and the buyers earn back the price.

governs.title: Overmighty subjects
governs.text: Governors and generals build power bases from estates, loyal commanders, wealth and popular support. Rulers rotate commands, split armies, raise parallel guards and hold hostages.

governs.title: Distribution
governs.text: Goods shared out by holding, office, need, work, share, equality or prestige. Markets, palace and temple stores, command economies, manors and gift economies.

governs.title: Citizens and foreigners
governs.text: Citizens, subjects, resident foreigners, protected minorities and the bound differ in their rights to property, office, arms and the courts. Citizenship is gained by descent, birthplace, residence, conversion, service, purchase or a grant.

governs.title: The licensed fool
governs.text: Jesters and satirists mock the ruler with permission. Tolerated satire calms the crowd, and suppressed satire turns into grievance.

name: Crowns Unclaimed
intro: Crowns Unclaimed brings claims to thrones, and the bloodlines that carry them, into the universe. Noble houses live on prestige, heirlooms, offices, feuds and special bloodlines. Titles run from lordship to empire, and claims arise from inheritance, marriage, conquest, divine favour or forgery. The gap between the map as it is held and the map as the law draws it is where claims and wars are born. Secret orders and houses steer marriages towards a goal across generations.
outcome: The dynastic politics of your universe run on the long reckoning of claims, marriages and bloodlines.

governs.title: Noble houses
governs.text: Prestige, heirlooms, offices, feuds, and bloodlines that may be long-lived, giant-blooded, god-blooded, cursed, fertile or gifted with prophecy. Houses marry for alliance, press claims despite the risks of marrying close kin, and split apart.

governs.title: Titles
governs.text: Lordships, counties, duchies, kingdoms and empires, as well as bishoprics, archbishoprics, the supreme seat, mercenary captaincies and guild masterships. A title is founded by holding most of its land, and is inherited, granted, usurped or restored.

governs.title: Right and might
governs.text: Land held long enough under another title passes to that title in law over time.

governs.title: Claims, unions and partitions
governs.text: Claims born of inheritance, marriage, conquest, divine favour, forgery or legal right fade if they are not pressed. A ruler who wears two crowns governs two realms at once, and partition laws divide realms among heirs. Succession follows primogeniture, seniority, election, tanistry, the second line, combat, divine choice or ultimogeniture.

governs.title: Heraldry
governs.text: Every house, realm, title, army and guild bears arms born of its deeds, its founder's wounds, its totems and its patron god. Arms are differenced for cadet branches and quartered for unions.

governs.title: Siblings against cousins
governs.text: Lineages sit inside clans, and clans inside tribes. Siblings fight cousins, the two unite against strangers, and the whole tribe unites against an outsider.

governs.title: The long plan
governs.text: Secret orders and houses steer marriages across generations towards divine blood, a gift of prophecy or the joining of claims. A love match or a barren marriage can undo a century of work.

name: The Iron Code
intro: The Iron Code gives the universe a working legal order. Laws decide heirs, punishments, taxes, who may be enslaved and whether magic is forbidden or licensed. Bills move forward on the balance between their backers and their opponents. Cases are settled on evidence, and evidence decays over time, so wrong verdicts grow out of bad evidence. When an oath sworn before the gods is broken, the god's wrath follows.
outcome: Justice and injustice in your universe both follow their own rules, and every verdict has a story behind it.

governs.title: Areas of law
governs.text: Succession, property, fiscal, penal, military, social, public health, magic and constitutional law. A law that clashes with the people's values breeds unrest.

governs.title: Lawmaking
governs.text: Bills advance on the balance of backers and opponents. Estates block bills with their privileges, and debates end in riots or compromise. A bill stuck too long fails and shames its champion.

governs.title: Legal systems
governs.text: Custom held in the elders' memory, written codes, sacred texts, binding precedent and oracles, or a mix of these. Under an oracle system a god answers the court, and that god may tell the truth, lie or stay silent.

governs.title: Evidence
governs.text: Witnesses, traces, documents, confessions, divination and magic. Witnesses can accuse, protect or keep silent. Evidence decays over time.

governs.title: Courts and trials
governs.text: Local, provincial, high and religious courts. Trial by judge, jury, combat or ordeal. Skilled advocates win cases, so the rich find better justice. Under precedent, every verdict binds the next. Clergy, guilds and foreigners may claim their own jurisdiction.

governs.title: Registers
governs.text: Registers of land titles, debts, sales, dowries and indentures.

governs.title: Crimes and punishments
governs.text: Crimes from theft to treason, witchcraft to mind theft. Punishments from fines to exile, branding to execution. Prisons breed gangs, diseases and new skills, and released convicts carry a stigma. Rulers pardon their friends and declare amnesties after civil wars. Debts can lead to bondage, prison or a jubilee.

governs.title: Oaths before the gods
governs.text: Oaths of fealty, vengeance, celibacy, pilgrimage, protection, silence and sworn kinship are taken with a god as witness. A broken oath brings the god's wrath, and kept oaths strengthen the gods of oaths.

name: Guilds and Estates
intro: Guilds and Estates organises the centres of power inside a realm. Guilds, priesthoods, warrior orders, peasant leagues, rebels, pirates, academies, secret societies and mercenary companies each pursue their own goals. Estates bargain for tax exemptions, monopolies, council seats and the right to bear arms. Trading companies, with their shares, overseas monopolies and hired armies, can grow into realms of their own.
outcome: Every decision a ruler makes passes through the balance of power inside the realm.

governs.title: Factions
governs.text: Factions from merchant and craft guilds to priesthoods, warrior orders to noble councils, peasant leagues to rebels, bandits to pirates, assassins to academies and secret societies. A faction can grow from a small band into a wide network.

governs.title: Goals and means
governs.text: Lower taxes, win a monopoly, put a claimant on the throne, repeal or pass a law, bring war or peace, win independence. To get there: lobbying, bribery, petitions, strikes, riots, coups, assassination, smuggling, raids, funding wars and recruiting members.

governs.title: Balance of power
governs.text: Inside every realm, the influence of the factions forms a balance that shapes every decision of the ruler. A guild monopoly sets prices and shuts out rivals, and smuggling rises to meet it.

governs.title: Estates and privileges
governs.text: Nobles, clergy, burghers, peasants and warriors bargain for tax exemption, monopolies, council seats, the right to bear arms and judicial immunity. Every privilege buys loyalty and puts a price on the throne.

governs.title: Parties and movements
governs.text: Movements for abolition, independence, religious revival, land reform, the franchise and peace find support in every class. Where there are councils they become parties, and where there are none, revolts.

governs.title: Companies with armies
governs.text: Trading companies own shares, overseas monopolies and hired armies. They can conquer, grow into realms of their own, or collapse onto their banks and shareholders.

governs.title: Guild ranks and the power of the common purse
governs.text: Guilds control apprenticeship, quality standards and secret techniques. Cooperatives, mutual aid and burial societies pool money for mills, boats, irrigation, insurance, burials and credit.

name: Pacts and Perfidy
intro: Pacts and Perfidy turns diplomacy into a system that runs on clauses, crises and bad faith. Treaties are built from clauses, from tribute to ceded land, from hostages to blood money, and the universe enforces them every epoch. Conquests, unjust wars and broken treaties alarm the neighbours, and past a certain point the neighbours band together. A demand starts a crisis with a clock running. A treacherous ruler signs a treaty already planning to break it.
outcome: Relations between realms play out with the calculations, trust and betrayals of real diplomacy.

governs.title: Treaties and clauses
governs.text: Peace, truces, defensive and offensive alliances, non-aggression, vassalage, tribute, marriage and trade pacts, and interworld treaties. Clauses from calls to arms to tribute, hostages to blood money, extradition to champions. The parties to a treaty are signatories, overlords, vassals and guarantors. Treaties stay in force, are fulfilled, broken or expire. When one is broken, the guarantors step in and the god who witnessed it punishes too.

governs.title: The coalition against you
governs.text: Conquests, unjust wars and broken treaties raise alarm in every realm that hears of them. Past a certain point the neighbours unite under a standing call-to-arms clause.

governs.title: Crises on the brink
governs.text: A demand starts a crisis with a clock running: cede land, release a vassal, convert or pay. Other realms take sides in return for a share of the terms and favours. At every escalation someone can back down, concede or let it come to war.

governs.title: Spheres of influence and subject states
governs.text: Great powers hold subject states in their spheres: vassals, tributaries, marches, personal unions, clients, colonies and protectorates. Each has its own obligations and its own wish for independence. Realms stand as hegemon, great power, minor power or client.

governs.title: Bad faith and secret deals
governs.text: A treacherous ruler signs a treaty already planning to break it, and the other side trusts only as far as it believes. At summits several parties bargain in rounds and strike secret side deals.

governs.title: The limits of diplomacy
governs.text: A realm can keep up only as many alliances, guarantees and embassies as its government and envoys can carry.

governs.title: The council of worlds
governs.text: Realms on different worlds vote on shared route security, embargoes and bans on void rites, and can sanction even a god's world.

name: Rise and Ruin
intro: Rise and Ruin adds long waves to history. Realms grow, stagnate, fall into crisis and collapse or recover in cycles that last centuries. Popular misery, elite overproduction and fiscal distress combine to drive up political stress. Elites who find no office lead movements and revolts. Solidarity grows strong on the frontier and fades over generations of luxury.
outcome: The rise and fall of empires follows the universe's own dynamics, not a script written in advance.

governs.title: The political stress gauge
governs.text: Population pressure, popular immiseration, elite overproduction and fiscal distress combine into a single measure of stress. As it rises, factions form, coups and revolts grow likely, and crowds riot more easily.

governs.title: Counter-elites
governs.text: When nobles, the wealthy and the credentialed outnumber the offices, titles and land, the surplus becomes ambitious people with nowhere to go, and they lead factions, movements and revolts.

governs.title: Long cycles
governs.text: Over centuries: growth, stagnation and inflation, crisis, then collapse or recovery. With no script written in advance, population falls, elites thin out, wages rise and the climb begins again.

governs.title: Solidarity
governs.text: Solidarity grows strong on frontiers facing very different peoples and fades over generations of luxury. It raises unity, morale and resistance to assimilation, which is why hard frontier peoples topple softened empires.

governs.title: Challenge and response
governs.text: Disasters, climate shifts, invasions, plagues and famines spur research, new institutions and solidarity. Too little challenge brings stagnation, too much brings collapse. A severe but survivable challenge draws the strongest response.

governs.title: Long plans
governs.text: Realms, cults, orders and gods pursue goals that span centuries: greening a desert world, breeding a bloodline, transforming a world, building a wonder or foreseeing the future. Offices and orders carry these plans on long after their authors die.

governs.title: The science of history
governs.text: Scholarly orders with statistics and a great archive foresee a realm's future through a noisy lens and steer it with small interventions, until a great person or a god steps in and breaks the forecast.

name: Couriers and Ciphers
intro: Couriers and Ciphers adds the journey of news to the universe. News does not spread in an instant: it travels by envoys, letters, heralds, signal fires, birds, magical sendings, dreams and networks. The delay depends on distance, road and season, and mountain passes close in winter. Letters can be intercepted on the way, forged or mistranslated. Ciphers protect letters, and codebreakers labour over them for seasons.
outcome: Realms make their decisions on incomplete, late or wrong information, and that alone gives rise to stories.

governs.title: Ways to send word
governs.text: Envoys, letters, heralds, signal fires, birds, magical sendings, dreams sent by a god, and networks. The delay depends on distance, road and season, and between worlds news travels as fast as the routes allow.

governs.title: What a message carries
governs.text: Offers, demands, threats, insults, notices of gifts, proclamations, reports, pleas and intelligence.

governs.title: Intercepted messages
governs.text: Every region with spies, bandits or enemy armies is a chance to lose a letter. Stolen messages yield intelligence, material for blackmail or forged replies.

governs.title: Forgery
governs.text: The forger's skill is tested against how well the recipient knows the sender's hand. A forged declaration of war can set two innocent realms against each other.

governs.title: Lost in translation
governs.text: Misreadings grow with the gap between languages, the number of clauses and the interpreter's skill. A misread clause turns into a bitter dispute long after the ink has dried.

governs.title: Envoys and etiquette
governs.text: An envoy's skill and bearing decide how the envoy is received. An envoy can be welcomed, insulted, imprisoned or killed. Killing an envoy is unthinkable almost everywhere and means war.

governs.title: Ciphers and codebreakers
governs.text: If you encipher your letters, whoever intercepts them learns only that you wrote something. Codebreakers work on captured messages for seasons. As long as you do not know your cipher is broken, every message you send is read.

governs.title: Signal towers and public opinion
governs.text: Fire towers, mirror towers, courier posts and sending stones shrink the realm, until someone burns or seizes them. Criers, sermons, pamphlets and propaganda shape public opinion about the ruler, the laws, wars, gods and ideologies.

name: Tongues of Rumour
intro: Tongues of Rumour follows the journey not of news but of rumour. As word spreads along trade routes, pilgrim roads, journeys and spy networks, it bends with distance and language. Inside a city, stories pass from friend to friend, from circles to gatherings, and every teller tilts the story to suit their own view. Reputation is kept separately in every community and read through that community's own morals.
outcome: The reputation of characters and realms comes less from what they really did than from what is told about them.

governs.title: Spreading rumours
governs.text: Word spreads along trade routes, pilgrim roads, journeys and spy networks, and bends with distance and the gap between languages. A town that hears of an approaching army raises its walls. Rumours that refuse to die become legends.

governs.title: Gossip networks
governs.text: Inside a city, stories spread from friend to friend, through circles and gatherings. Every teller can tilt a story to suit their own view of its subject, so the palace and the harbour hear different scandals.

governs.title: Axes of reputation
governs.text: Heroism, honour, cruelty, piety, generosity, wisdom, cunning, renown for skill and troublemaking. Every community keeps these separately and reads them through its own morals. A massacre is cruelty to the victims and heroism to some conquerors.

governs.title: Spending reputation
governs.text: Rulers spend their reputation. Prestige buys the passing of laws, piety the backing of the clergy, and dread the silence of the opposition for a while. Tyranny builds up with unjust acts and turns vassals against the ruler.

governs.title: Secrets for sale
governs.text: Factions, cults, scholars and even beasts value certain knowledge: techniques, hidden places, maps and prophecies. A secret sells for wealth, favour or renown, but every sale cheapens it.

governs.title: False heroes
governs.text: Deeds must be credited to someone. A vain rival can claim your dragon, until the true hunter produces the beast's tongue. A claim can be true, shared or false. A claim can be verified or exposed. Exposure brings scandal, a duel or punishment, yet the chronicle may still honour the impostor.

name: Velvet Daggers
intro: Velvet Daggers brings intrigue into the universe. Everyone has a secret: an affair, a bastard, a murder, a heresy, membership of a hidden cult or a pact with an outer being. Secrets become hooks, and hooks become forced obedience. Schemes recruit agents, gather strength and strike. Every epoch a scheme's secrecy is tested against the counter-intelligence of the target's court. Even nature can become a weapon: pests released, fields burned, soil salted by night.
outcome: Beneath the courts and cities, a shadow game plays out by its own rules.

governs.title: Secrets
governs.text: Affairs, illegitimate children, murders, heresies, hidden cult membership, debts, crimes, cowardice in battle, hidden illness, false identities, pacts with outer beings, true parentage, broken oaths, ecosabotage, broken ciphers and true history. Every secret has those who know it and consequences it will bring if it comes out.

governs.title: Hooks and favours
governs.text: A hook born of a secret, a debt, a favour, a hostage or a true name forces obedience: a marriage, an abdication, support, a vote or a law. Weak hooks are spent when used, strong ones remain. Rescues, votes and aid create favour debts, and refusing a favour when it is called in costs honour.

governs.title: Living under other names
governs.text: Spies, the blood-cursed, exiles, impostors and those with hidden powers carry false identities. Investigations, careless slips or a familiar face give them away.

governs.title: Schemes
governs.text: Murder, abduction, seduction, persuasion, fabricated claims, fabricated hooks, relic theft, coups, well poisoning, framing, elopement, secret conversion, wedding sabotage and freeing prisoners. Schemes move through recruiting, preparation and execution. Agents are won through money, ideology, blackmail or vanity.

governs.title: Discovery
governs.text: Every epoch a scheme's secrecy is tested against the counter-intelligence of the target's court. An exposed scheme reveals its agents and leaves lasting memories. Mole hunts can catch spies, clear them, purge them or drive them to defect.

governs.title: Timing
governs.text: Night and fog raise the odds of success and hide witnesses, storms break off pursuit, festival crowds give both cover and more eyes, and a plague panic distracts the watch.

governs.title: Ecosabotage
governs.text: Releasing pests, burning fields, poisoning a fishery, secretly diverting a river or salting the soil by night. The damage spreads through the real ecology.

name: Shadow Networks
intro: Shadow Networks organises espionage into cells, motives and operations. Agents, handlers, dead drops and safe houses work under cover as merchants, priests or envoys. A captured agent can give away only their own cell. Money, ideology, blackmail or vanity decide an agent's loyalty and the risk of playing both sides. Paranoid spymasters accuse the innocent, and every purge sparks new defections. Even the gods use spies.
outcome: The secret wars between realms follow the logic of a real world of intelligence.

governs.title: Cell networks
governs.text: Agents, handlers, dead drops and safe houses. Agents work under cover as merchants, priests, envoys or beggars. A captured agent can give away only their own cell. Flat networks are fast but fragile. Networks can belong to realms, factions, cults or communities.

governs.title: Motives
governs.text: Money, ideology, blackmail and vanity. The motive decides loyalty and the risk of playing both sides. True believers are the most reliable agents and the hardest to turn.

governs.title: Operations
governs.text: Stealing knowledge, sabotage, assassination, incitement, gathering intelligence, blackmail and counterfeiting. Spies burn granaries, weaken walls, poison wells and set fires.

governs.title: Mole hunts
governs.text: Paranoid spymasters accuse the innocent. A mole hunt can catch a spy, clear one, or turn into a purge or a defection. Every purge costs loyal officers and drives more defections, which deepens the paranoia.

governs.title: Defectors and double agents
governs.text: Captured agents can be turned to feed false information, or traded. Defectors carry their secrets across the border and need protection.

governs.title: Death by design
governs.text: Blade, poison, a staged accident, deliberate infection or a curse. Whether a murder is noticed depends on the physician's skill and the medicine of the age.

governs.title: Spies of the gods
governs.text: Scrying rites, dream intrusion and servant spies cross any distance. Wards and the sphere of a rival god block them.

name: Fog of Belief
intro: Fog of Belief makes every decision-maker in the universe see the world not as it is but as far as they know it. Every ruler, commander and merchant carries their own beliefs: the size of an enemy army, a rival's treasury, an heir's health, a god's favour. Every belief has a level of confidence, a date and a source. Knowledge fades as it ages, and stale beliefs lead to fatal decisions.
outcome: The mistakes, miscalculations and surprises of your universe arise on their own from what characters do not know.

governs.title: Belief stores
governs.text: Every actor who makes decisions carries their own beliefs. Every belief has a level of confidence, a date and a source.

governs.title: Ways of knowing
governs.text: Seeing with one's own eyes, letters, rumours, spies, scouts, records and deception. Records exist only where someone can write.

governs.title: Fading knowledge
governs.text: Confidence falls over time, and stale beliefs lead to fatal decisions. The rival you believe bankrupt may have paid off their debts last spring with a dragon's hoard.

governs.title: Deception
governs.text: Feints, false campfires, planted rumours and forged letters write lies straight into a rival's picture of the world.

governs.title: Markets in the fog
governs.text: Merchants trade on the price gaps they believe in. Where news arrives fast, prices draw together; where it arrives slowly, they stay apart. Insurers price risk, and speculators hoard, by belief.

governs.title: The gap laid bare
governs.text: You can switch between the world any realm believes in and the real world. As the Creator you can show an actor the truth or plant a false belief in them. Agents that play mortals see only what that mortal knows.

depth.text: 15 sources of belief, from observation to deception.
Confidence, date and source for every belief.

name: Steel and Banner
intro: Steel and Banner turns armies into forces made of real people, real weapons and real logistics. Soldiers are equipped with the weapons and armour their peoples forged before the war. Every region can feed only so many mouths. A unit's strength, cohesion and discipline are tracked separately. Commanders win renown with traits earned from their battle records. Regiments earn names, nicknames and battle honours.
outcome: Every army reflects the economy, technology and history of the people that raised it.

governs.title: Unit kinds
governs.text: Unit kinds from infantry to archers, cavalry to vehicle crews, war beasts to sappers, casters to exotic units, air and space units to special forces. Each has its own melee, ranged attack, defence, speed and morale.

governs.title: Equipment
governs.text: Every unit is equipped with the weapons and armour its people forged before the war: from hide to plate, enchanted armour to energy shields. When the army disbands, the soldiers go home, minus the dead.

governs.title: Hunger before battle
governs.text: Every region can feed only so many mouths. Armies over the limit strip the land and earn hatred. A winter campaign in the mountains in heavy armour can destroy an army without a single battle. Armies march, forage, entrench, besiege, garrison, raid or retreat.

governs.title: Strength, cohesion and discipline
governs.text: Three values tracked separately in every unit. A unit whose cohesion breaks routs even at full strength. Drilled professionals hold where levies scatter.

governs.title: Commanders
governs.text: Skill in fire, shock, manoeuvre, siege and logistics, plus traits earned from battle records, from aggressive assaulter to defensive genius, cavalry master to winter campaigner. Armies have commander, sub-commander, quartermaster, standard bearer and surgeon roles.

governs.title: Formations, engines and engineering
governs.text: Battle formations such as line, column, wedge, square, loose order, shieldwall and entrenched order. Siege engines built from plans that rivals can steal. Engineers who throw pontoon bridges and dig earthworks.

governs.title: Regiments and veterans
governs.text: Units raised from the same region earn names, nicknames and honours on their banners, and remember their massacres. Veterans receive land in new colonies or a pension.

governs.title: Mercenaries and mutinies
governs.text: Mercenary contracts can stay in force, go unpaid, change sides or end. Unpaid soldiers grumble, refuse orders, depose their commanders, and turn to banditry or treason.

name: Field of Glory
intro: Field of Glory turns battles into events that unfold phase by phase. A battle opens with scouting and moves through the commanders' plans, missile fire, the charge, melee, rites and miracles, the pursuit and the aftermath. Terrain, weather, tactics and morale decide the outcome. Three hundred in a narrow pass can hold back thirty thousand for a while. An eclipse can scatter an army that reads it as an evil omen.
outcome: Every battle has its own course, its own heroes and its own turning point.

governs.title: Phases of battle
governs.text: Scouting, planning, command, missile fire, the charge, melee, reserves, rites, pursuit, salvage and the aftermath. A patron god can step into the fight, and that attention can draw a rival god in too.

governs.title: Terrain and weather
governs.text: A pass strengthens the defender, a marsh slows heavy troops, streets swallow cavalry. Fog blinds archers and makes ambushes more likely, and an eclipse scatters the armies of peoples who read it as an evil omen.

governs.title: Tactics
governs.text: Holding the line, frontal assault, double envelopment, feigned retreat, flanking cavalry, missile attrition, the shield wall and more. Every tactic has a counter and ground that suits it.

governs.title: Frontage
governs.text: Only so many soldiers can fight at once. Reserves wait for the front line to tire. A square stops cavalry but melts under arrows.

governs.title: Steps of morale
governs.text: Steady, shaken, wavering, routing, broken and rallied. Panic spreads to neighbouring units, standards and priests rally the wavering, and orders arrive late or garbled when the army speaks more than one language.

governs.title: The physics of slaughter
governs.text: In melee only the front rank kills, but massed arrows and spells hit the whole enemy, so concentrating force pays off many times over. Plate, chitin and stone skin turn blows aside.

governs.title: After the battle
governs.text: The dead, the wounded, the maimed and the captured are counted separately. Without field surgeons the wounded die that season. Captives can be ransomed, enslaved, sacrificed, put to work, exchanged or set free.

depth.text: 12 battle phases and 25 tactics.
6 morale states.
7 battle outcomes, from decisive victory to massacre.
7 kinds of casualty and 10 possible fates for captives.
6 kinds of field and siege outcome

name: Walls Will Fall
intro: Walls Will Fall turns sieges into struggles that last weeks and seasons. There are five ways into a city: blockade, bombardment, mining, assault or negotiation. Defenders sally out to burn siege towers, repair breaches, ration their stores and wait for relief. Beneath the walls, miners and counterminers duel in the dark. Hunger and disease strike both the city and the besiegers' camp.
outcome: Every siege has its own drama, and a city that falls never forgets who took it.

governs.title: Ways to take a city
governs.text: Blockade, bombardment, mining, assault and negotiation. Siege engines are chosen for the stone of the walls, and mines for the rock and soil beneath them. An assault is a battle fought on the walls.

governs.title: Siege works
governs.text: Lines of circumvallation, siege towers, rams, mines, countermines and ladders.

governs.title: The defender's answer
governs.text: Sallies that burn siege towers, masons who patch breaches from the stone stores, rationing and the hope of relief.

governs.title: Hunger and disease
governs.text: Rationing leads to famine, and famine to taboos that only some peoples will break. Disease spreads through both the city and the besiegers' camp according to water, sanitation and season.

governs.title: Treachery at the gate
governs.text: Hunger wears down the garrison's courage and raises the risk of riots in the streets. A faction with an old grudge may simply open the gate.

governs.title: Sack or mercy
governs.text: The victor's doctrine and the commander's traits decide. A sack takes the treasury, the holy relics and the people, burns whole districts and brings infamy. The city never forgets who took it. The victor may show mercy, sack the city or raze it to the ground.

governs.title: Fleets at the harbour mouth
governs.text: Only a fleet can starve a coastal city from the sea.

governs.title: Lines of stone
governs.text: Castles and walled cities control the regions around them. An invader must besiege each fortress or march past it and risk having the supply line cut, so lines of fortresses shape every invasion.

depth.text: 8 ways to wage a siege and 14 kinds of siege work.
9 defender actions.

depth.label: Defender actions
values: sending out those who cannot fight

depth.text: 5 stages of starvation, from rationing to a broken taboo.
6 choices after a city falls, including mercy, sack and razing.

name: Theatre of War
intro: Theatre of War lifts war from single battles to whole campaigns. Army groups, armies, corps, divisions and brigades are run from their headquarters. Supply flows like a river: cut one depot and every army it feeds begins to starve. Offensives reach their culminating point as supply lines stretch. War goals, casus belli and peace terms are balanced by a war score. On the home front, support for the war rises and falls.
outcome: Wars play out from their first spark to the peace table, in every political, logistical and social dimension.

governs.title: Chain of command
governs.text: Army groups, armies, corps, divisions and brigades, each run from a headquarters with its own staff. Couriers and signal networks extend a commander's reach, and units beyond it fight on under the orders they already have.

governs.title: Supply
governs.text: Depots, carts, pack animals, porters, barges, ships and sky barges carry supply at a limited rate. Cut a single depot or river line and every army it feeds goes hungry.

governs.title: Culmination
governs.text: Offensives outrun their supply as their lines stretch. Generals with a head for logistics see the limit coming.

governs.title: War goals
governs.text: Conquering a region, seizing a settlement, pressing a claim, forcing conversion, taking tribute, making a vassal, liberating, destroying a cult, seizing a resource or a nexus, humiliating and taking revenge. Occupied land pays taxes and gives soldiers, and its resistance grows with every atrocity.

governs.title: Casus belli and peace
governs.text: Causes for war run from a claim to holy war, from blood feud to trade dispute and unpaid debt, or there is bare conquest with no justification at all. Every peace term costs war score: ceded land, tribute, hostages, reparations. Wars end in victory, conquest, tribute, exhaustion, peace, white peace, betrayal or a miracle.

governs.title: The home front
governs.text: Support for the war rises with propaganda and a just cause, and falls with taxes, losses and maimed veterans in the streets. Weary peoples press for peace.

governs.title: Negotiation
governs.text: Bluffs and insults before battle, truces for the harvest and for burying the dead, surrender terms with the honours of war and prisoner exchanges. Parleys, truces, surrenders, exchanges, safe conducts and fraternisation can be kept, ended, broken or repudiated. A sworn word that is broken is remembered.

16 supply carriers.

19 kinds of peace term and 11 different ways a war can end.

values: both sides on the same front

name: Admiralty
intro: Admiralty ties war at sea, in the sky and in space to real physics and real design. The fleet with the wind at its back chooses the terms of battle, while galleys ignore the wind at the cost of their rowers' strength. Round shot holes hulls, chain shot cuts rigging, grapeshot cuts down crews and fire pots set sails alight. Ships are designed with their hulls, sails, holds and wards.
outcome: Every clash at sea, in the sky or in space grows out of the ships' own designs and conditions.

governs.title: Wind and sailing
governs.text: Close hauled, reaching, running, under oars and in irons. The fleet with the wind at its back chooses the battle.

governs.title: Damage where it lands
governs.text: Round shot, chain shot, grapeshot and fire. Fire spreads through deck timber, and a single spark in the magazine ends a ship.

governs.title: Boarding and prizes
governs.text: Marines fight boarding actions, galleys strike with the ram. Ships that strike their colours become prizes, prize crews thin out the victor's deck, and prize money flows to the crews' households.

governs.title: Command of sea and sky
governs.text: Armies cross water safely only under naval supremacy, and landings on defended shores are bloody. Skyships and flying mounts win the sky for scouting, raids on supply columns and siege bombardment.

governs.title: Designed hulls
governs.text: Craft from rafts to longships, from galleons to bone hulls, from living ships to generation ships. Each is designed with hulls, sails, sky and void sails, holds, wards and caster stations. Land, water, underwater, air, space, gas giant, underground and planar craft. Propulsion from oar and sail to steam, and from electricity to solar sails and engines that fold space.

governs.title: Crew
governs.text: Gunners, riggers, marines, officers and rowers.

governs.title: Stars and chronometers
governs.text: A compass works only on worlds with a magnetic field, an astrolabe needs astronomy, and a marine chronometer gives longitude. Lost ships drift to unknown shores.

governs.title: The admiralty board
governs.text: Admirals compete with generals in council for the treasury, and naval treaties set tonnage limits by ship class. Breaking those limits is a scheme in its own right.

governs.title: Battle in every domain
governs.text: Ship-to-ship battles at sea, in the sky and in space. Weapons choose the section they strike, and fire, flooding, loss of air and loss of power spread from one to the next.

name: Blade and Honour
intro: Blade and Honour turns duels into fights fought move by move. Every move weighs weapon skill, reach, armour, the footing under the day's weather, draining stamina and pain. A spear keeps a sword at bay until the swordsman closes the distance. Duels end in surrender, disarming, a crippling wound or death, and the loser carries that defeat for life.
outcome: Every duel is a scene you can follow step by step, and by its end an eye, a hand or a life may be lost.

governs.title: Moves
governs.text: Every duel is made of several moves. Weapon skill, reach, armour, footing, stamina and pain shape each one.

governs.title: Strike, feint and parry
governs.text: Fighters choose to strike at a chosen target, feint, block, parry, dodge or grapple. Whether a parry meets the blow depends on how well the defender reads the attack.

governs.title: Grappling and throws
governs.text: Seizing a limb or a weapon, throwing, choking an opponent until they pass out, twisting a joint until it breaks, or, in some cultures, biting when all else fails.

governs.title: Lance and horse
governs.text: A couched lance strikes with the mass and speed of the mount. The horse is a target too, and a falling horse crushes its rider.

governs.title: Lasting wounds
governs.text: The loser does not simply limp away “badly wounded”. They lose an eye, a hand or a leg, and carry that loss for life.

governs.title: Reasons to fight
governs.text: Duels of war, duels of honour born of a grudge, trial by combat, champions whose single combat ends a war, and duels between gods that leave divine wounds behind.

governs.title: Mercy on the ground
governs.text: A fighter who falls fights at a disadvantage. The victor's mercy decides whether they live, and honour decides whether a surrender is accepted.

governs.title: A record of every move
governs.text: Every duel is recorded step by step: each blow with its weapon, its target and the wound it left.

depth.text: 7 duel contexts, from war to the gods.
9 ways a duel ends, from surrender to death.
9 strike styles, from normal strikes and trampling to aerial attacks and low blows.

name: Blood Feud
intro: Blood Feud adds blood feuds and captivity to the universe. A blood feud is the memory of kin killed between two houses or two peoples. The wronged raid, assassinate, demand blood money or escalate the feud into a war of vengeance, and every death adds to the reckoning. Pursuits and raids take whole cohorts captive. Heirs raised as hostages in an enemy court absorb its culture and its memories.
outcome: Past violence lives on for generations and gives rise to new stories.

governs.title: The blood ledger
governs.text: A blood feud is the memory of kin killed between two houses or communities. The wronged raid, assassinate, demand blood money or escalate. Every death adds to the ledger.

governs.title: What ends a feud
governs.text: Blood money law, marriages, a common enemy, a priest preaching peace, and memory slowly fading over generations. Without these, a feud outlives those who started it. Feuds close through mediation, by fading or by coming to an end.

governs.title: Captives by the thousand
governs.text: Pursuits and raids take whole cohorts captive. Captives are ransomed, enslaved where the law allows, sacrificed where doctrine demands, put to work, exchanged or set free. Named captives can escape, be executed, change sides or be rescued.

governs.title: Hostage heirs
governs.text: Child heirs raised in an enemy court absorb its culture and memories. Depending on their temperament, they return as friendly or vengeful rulers.

governs.title: Stolen children
governs.text: Raiders carry off children. Unless their memory is strong, they forget where they came from and become soldiers of their captors or famous turncoats. Their kin plan rescues and searches.

governs.title: Slave soldiers
governs.text: Enslaved cohorts fight with low morale, desert easily and may turn on their masters mid-battle when their own people stand against them.

governs.title: Parole
governs.text: A captured officer can go free by swearing never to fight again. Breaking that parole is breaking an oath, and the shame follows them home.

depth.text: 12 actions in a blood feud
8 states of a blood feud.
10 possible fates for captives and 10 states for named captives.
4 kinds of feud level
3 kinds of feud party

name: Tenets of Flame
intro: Tenets of Flame gives faiths real doctrine. Every faith has a few core tenets, and each one has a real effect. Sacred suffering honours the maimed, while purity of body counts them unclean. Celibate clergy found no households, and human sacrifice horrifies the neighbours. Zeal rises with persecution, martyrs and miracles, and fades with prosperity and scandal. Doctrine drifts over time and splits into heresies.
outcome: The universe's religions are living structures with their own doctrines, institutions and schisms.

governs.title: Tenets
governs.text: Tenets that run from pacifism to holy war, from asceticism to sacred suffering, from purity of body to ancestor worship, and from human and animal sacrifice to celibate clergy and missionary work. Every faith holds several tenets, and each has real effects.

governs.title: Zeal
governs.text: Persecution, martyrs, miracles, holy war victories and plagues raise zeal. Prosperity, scandals and prophecies that never come true quench it. Zeal that climbs too high turns into inquisitions, iconoclasm or crusades.

governs.title: Clergy, tithes and holdings
governs.text: High priests, priests, monks and inquisitors. The tithe feeds them and funds alms, war chests and the monasteries that keep knowledge alive through dark ages. Temples, lands, holy relics, holy places and monasteries are the faith's holdings.

governs.title: Heresy and schism
governs.text: In the hands of a creative theologian, doctrine drifts and splits into a tree of heresies. Orthodoxy chooses between inquisition and tolerance, and councils vote on doctrines and saints.

governs.title: Missions on the trade roads
governs.text: Preachers travel with caravans. Conversion depends on how well the doctrine fits the culture, on the missionary's skill and on the miracles behind them.

governs.title: Church and crown
governs.text: Divine kingship unites throne and altar. Elsewhere, priests and rulers contend for the right to appoint, and excommunication strips a ruler of legitimacy. Gods can reveal a new tenet.

governs.title: Sanctuary
governs.text: Temples shelter criminals, runaway slaves and defeated rivals. The pursuer must besiege, bargain or wait, because violating sanctuary is sacrilege.

depth.text: 28 kinds of tenet.
Open-ended clergy offices and 10 kinds of religious holding.
12 kinds of fanaticism, including inquisition, iconoclasm and crusade.

depth.label: Kinds of fanaticism
values: pilgrim zeal that leaves everything behind

name: Prophets of the End
intro: Prophets of the End brings the life of faith outside the temple into the universe. Devout mortals with strong intuition see visions, gather followers outside the clergy and found orders or heresies. Prophecies of the end, signs in the sky and deepening misery give rise to movements whose followers sell their land, stop working and wait for the end. When the god stays silent, doctrine falls into crisis. Temples empty over time and fill again when disaster strikes.
outcome: Faith is a living, unpredictable force that steers the history of the universe.

governs.title: Mystics
governs.text: Devout mortals with strong intuition experience visions, states of union, voices and trances. Their path runs from seeking to vision, from reverence to persecution, and from founding a movement to losing their faith. Their contact is real only if a god chooses to answer.

governs.title: Apocalyptic movements
governs.text: Prophecies of the end, signs in the sky and deepening misery give rise to movements. Movements stir, gather, keep vigil, march, set a new date, become a sect or disperse.

governs.title: When the day comes and goes
governs.text: Believers disperse, set a new date or become a sect that will outlive its prophets.

governs.title: The silent god
governs.text: When plague, famine, defeat or disaster strikes believers and their god gives no sign, doctrine falls into crisis. Theologians argue, a new doctrine explains the suffering as a test, and people turn to another faith or drift away from belief.

governs.title: Rites that truly protect
governs.text: Birth blessing, initiation, marriage and last rites guard the soul's path after death, protect children from possession and keep the dead from wandering in unrest.

governs.title: Emptying temples
governs.text: Literacy, prosperity, city life, new theories of nature and gods who stay silent too long wear faith down. Disasters, wars and miracles fill the temples again.

depth.text: 7 kinds of mystical experience and 7 states of a mystic.

depth.label: Mystical experiences
values: oracle speech in words not one's own

depth.text: 7 stages of apocalyptic movements.
8 events that bring on the god's silence and 6 possible ends to the crisis.
8 sacraments and 5 kinds of protection.

depth.label: Sacrament protections
values: Guiding the soul on its way

name: Beyond the Veil
intro: Beyond the Veil makes what lies beyond death a real place. The realm of the dead divides into layers: paradise, plain, torment, oblivion or a faith's own hall of warriors. Souls are weighed, and their path is set by their patron's doctrine, their funeral rites and divine favour. The unburied dead wander, vengeful spirits spread unrest, and spirits possess living bodies. Every faith teaches an afterlife, and the truth may be different.
outcome: Death is not an end but the next chapter of the universe.

governs.title: Layers of the dead
governs.text: Paradise, plain, torment, oblivion, the hall of warriors and the hall of ancestors, each with its own conditions of entry. Every realm of the dead holds its own population.

governs.title: The weighing
governs.text: The patron god's doctrine of judgement (deeds, faith, rite, favour or none), the funeral rite and divine favour set the soul's path. Renown, honour, faith, violence and unthinkable acts all count. The unburied dead wander.

governs.title: Earned rebirth
governs.text: A soul returns only through an open gate: a tenet, a law of nature, a rite or a god's hand. It is reborn into a people, into a household or according to its merit, and carries faint memories of its life.

governs.title: Ghosts
governs.text: Restless, vengeful, grieving, bound, noisy, protective and possessing ghosts. Each needs its own remedy: a memorial stone carved with its name, a proper funeral or an exorcism. Spirits can be bound to a place, an object, a structure, a creature or a person.

governs.title: Possession and its cure
governs.text: A spirit can possess a living body and take the place of the host's mind, until an exorcism drives it out.

governs.title: Ancestors and soul eaters
governs.text: Honoured ancestors bring the household luck and courage, and grow restless when the offerings stop. Soul eaters devour the dead and starve a god of its believers.

governs.title: The afterlife surprise
governs.text: Every faith teaches an afterlife, and the truth may be different. Souls who find their faith was wrong suffer the shock of revelation. The dead who return in dreams can tell the living the truth.

depth.text: Open-ended afterlife layers and 9 afterlife doctrines.

depth.label: Afterlife doctrines
values: the dead remaining among the living

name: Spirits of Hearth and River
intro: Spirits of Hearth and River settles local spirits into every corner of the universe. Rivers, springs, groves, hearths, crossroads, mountains and cities can each hold a spirit with its own temperament, its own tastes and a running account of offerings and favours with the people. Pleased spirits bring fertility, safe passage, good hunting and luck at the hearth; offended ones bring misfortune and floods. Spirits hold rank in a celestial bureaucracy, and mortals send them written petitions.
outcome: Beneath the gods, the spiritual map of the universe is full of local powers that change from village to village.

governs.title: Spirits of place
governs.text: Rivers, springs, lakes, wells, shores, groves, forests, mountains, caves, crossroads, wilds, fields, cities and hearths can hold a spirit. Each spirit has its own temperament, its own tastes and a running account of offerings and favours with the people.

governs.title: Offending a spirit
governs.text: Pollution, felling forests, an unpaid offering or a broken taboo bring misfortune, floods and disease. Pleased spirits grant fertility, safe passage, good hunting and luck at the hearth.

governs.title: The celestial bureaucracy
governs.text: Hearth gods, river gods and city gods hold rank beneath the gods and foreign gods: hearth, local, city, province and ministry. Mortals file written petitions for healing, harvest, fertility, safe passage, prosperity or a lawsuit. Petitions are filed, delayed, granted, denied, appealed or dismissed.

governs.title: Promotion and dismissal
governs.text: Spirits rise through good service, growing worship and resolved petitions, and are demoted or dismissed for neglect. A village can lodge a complaint about its river god with the city god.

governs.title: Spirits of feeling
governs.text: Where magic runs strong, the fear on a battlefield, the joy at a festival, the grief at a funeral and the rage of a crowd become spirits that amplify that feeling.

governs.title: Teachers from beyond
governs.text: Ancestors, ghosts and spirits of place teach through dreams, visions and possession: songs, arts, rites, lost techniques, true names, prophecies, the way to buried treasure, languages and histories. Teachings can be given, blocked or sold.

name: Hex and Hunt
intro: Hex and Hunt adds folk belief and witch hunts to the universe. Every culture reads luck into its calendar, signs, numbers and gestures. Amulets truly work where they are enchanted or blessed; elsewhere they only comfort the wearer. An unexplained illness, a withered crop or a dead child sets people looking for someone to blame, and belief, grudges and social distance choose who. Plague, famine and war turn a single accusation into a chain of hunts.
outcome: The universe's fears produce their own victims and their own stories.

governs.title: Signs of luck
governs.text: Days, numbers, signs, gestures, places, acts and people. Every culture reads luck from them for harvest, health, birth, travel or war.

governs.title: Amulets
governs.text: Amulets of protection, fertility, luck and healing. They truly work where they are enchanted or blessed; elsewhere they only comfort the wearer, which is a real effect too.

governs.title: Misfortunes and their explanations
governs.text: Illness, crop loss, a child's death, livestock death, an accident or bad luck. People blame chance, a known cause, witchcraft, a curse, a god, a spirit, an ancestor, an omen, fate, an enemy's scheme, impurity or a broken oath. The answer may be a rite, an offering, an amulet, an accusation, a purification or a safety custom.

governs.title: Who is the witch
governs.text: Belief, grudges and social distance pick the culprit: the envied neighbour, the widow, the stranger.

governs.title: From accusation to ordeal
governs.text: Diviners and rumours name the culprit, and then come trials, ordeals, exile or murder. The accused may be cleared, punished, exiled or killed.

governs.title: The hunt spreads
governs.text: Plague, famine and war, joined with zealous inquisitors, turn one accusation into a chain. Hunts leave behind memories, chronicles and the vengeful ghosts of those wrongly killed.

governs.title: Real witches
governs.text: Where rites and curses exist, some of the accused really do practise magic. The engine knows who, and you see every true and every false accusation.

name: Omens and Oracles
intro: Omens and Oracles makes prophecy a working part of the universe. A prophecy states its condition plainly: a death, the fall of a city, a child to be born into a house, an eclipse. The moment the universe meets that condition, the prophecy comes true. Believers act for it or against it: children born under the comet press their claims, the king turns paranoid and infants die. Seers glimpse possible futures, but they can be wrong, because others act on the prophecy too.
outcome: Prophecies become story engines that fulfil themselves or come to nothing.

governs.title: Prophecies that can come true
governs.text: Every prophecy has a clear condition and comes true the moment the universe meets it. Prophecies, legends and story hooks connect to one another.

governs.title: Self-fulfilling fates
governs.text: Believers act for or against the prophecy. When its time runs out, the seer loses standing or the prophecy is reinterpreted.

governs.title: Ways to read the gods
governs.text: Augury, haruspicy, astrology, oracles, lots and dream reading. Each gives true knowledge only where a god answers, a seer has the gift or the laws of nature allow it; elsewhere it is only noise. People consult them before battles, campaigns, weddings, coronations and harvests, and the answer comes out auspicious, inauspicious or unclear.

governs.title: Seers and blind spots
governs.text: The gifted glimpse possible futures. Rival seers blind each other, and outer beings appear in no foresight. Foresight comes from a power, a method of divination, a god or a made oracle, and it comes true, fails or clouds over.

governs.title: Born under a sign
governs.text: Every mortal carries the sky of the moment they were born. Where the stars truly hold power, the sign shapes temperament and fortune; elsewhere it is only a belief, but belief moves people too.

governs.title: Dreams
governs.text: Ordinary dreams, nightmares, longings, prophetic dreams, visitations and shared dreams. Nightmares recur, dream readers get it wrong, and a dream that a king takes for an omen of war can start a war.

depth.text: 11 methods of divination and 4 sources of validity.
10 kinds of question and 3 kinds of answer.
5 sources of foresight and 4 foresight states.
8 kinds of dream and open-ended dream readings.

name: The Arcanum
intro: The Arcanum gives magic a grammar. Every rite pairs a technique with a form: creating, perceiving, transforming, destroying, controlling, binding or warding, in a field that runs from fire to time and from the void to light. Range stretches from a touch to a whole world, and duration from an instant to forever. Magic reads the weather and the world: rain weakens a fire rite, and a dry forest turns a fire rite into a wildfire.
outcome: The universe's magic is a coherent system with its own rules, costs and limits.

governs.title: The grammar of magic
governs.text: Techniques from creating to mimicking, forms from fire to spirit and from time to space. Ranges from touch to a whole world, durations from an instant to permanent, targets from a single person to a region.

governs.title: Vis and the black market
governs.text: Magical resources of every form, from fire vis to death vis, gather at sites of power, are harvested from creatures and drawn from natural phenomena. Where magic is outlawed, they flow through the black market.

governs.title: Resistance and counterspells
governs.text: Will, discipline, faith, sanctity, material, dampeners, distance and opposing sources resist a rite. Counterspells, dispels and wards meet in a contest of power.

governs.title: Magic that meets the world
governs.text: Wet targets conduct storm rites, rain weakens fire and strengthens water, and a dry forest turns a fire rite into a wildfire.

governs.title: Tongue, hand and breath
governs.text: Rites need words, gestures, writing, song, dance, materials or the mind. A caster whose tongue is cut out can still write, and a blinded caster can still chant. Captive casters are gagged, bound at the hands and blindfolded.

governs.title: Material magic
governs.text: Metals that empower the gifted, crystals that store a technique, salt that keeps spirits away. Materials are used by consuming, wearing, inscribing or grinding them. Enchanted items hold charges and refill at a site of power, with vis or with the cycle of the moon.

governs.title: Orders and traditions
governs.text: Magical orders enforce their rules in their own courts and found communities with laboratories and libraries. Every tradition rests on a theory, and the closer it is to the truth, the stronger it is.

name: Forbidden Arts
intro: Forbidden Arts explores the dark side of magic. Blood rites spend the caster's own body or a captive's life; void rites spend sanity and let the darkness leak in. Necromancers turn the battle dead into armies that know no fear. A lock of hair, a drop of blood or a name links a rite to its target. Casters and those who live on ley lines slowly change. A failed rite can wound the caster, drive them mad or let something summoned slip free.
outcome: Power always comes at a price, and the greatest powers demand the heaviest prices.

governs.title: Blood and void
governs.text: Blood rites spend the caster's body or a captive's life; void rites spend sanity and make the darkness leak in faster. They bring infamy, and desperate, merciless casters reach for them first.

governs.title: Towers of the dead
governs.text: Necromancers turn the battle dead into armies that know no fear and need no food. These armies rot unless they are fed with essence or spirit.

governs.title: Curses and transformations
governs.text: Dark rites lay curses, blessings and bodily transformations on their targets.

governs.title: A lock of hair
governs.text: Hair, blood, a name, a portrait or a fragment links a rite to its target. The stronger the link, the deeper the rite reaches. The careful burn their hair and hide their true names.

governs.title: Corruption
governs.text: Casters, those who live on ley lines and those who carry enchanted items slowly change: an uncanny look, attunement, madness, unnaturally long life.

governs.title: Decades bought
governs.text: Elixirs and rites hold off ageing at the cost of rare resources, corruption and growing dependence. Cut off an ancient caster's source and the years come due.

governs.title: Backlash
governs.text: A failed rite can wound, drive mad, widen the leak from the void or let something summoned escape. A failed storm rite can become a storm that never ends.

11 kinds of magical hazard, from injury to drawing attention.

name: Walkers of Myth
intro: Walkers of Myth turns legends into living forces. With every telling, a legend leans toward the teller's values and moves people to act: a legend of the king's return strengthens a claimant who fits it, and a legend of a haunted place keeps settlers away. Heroes enter a god's palace, the realm of the dead, a dream world or a holy place and face its trials. Taboos laid at birth and true names shape destinies.
outcome: The universe's myths are both stories that are told and forces that change the world.

governs.title: Living legends
governs.text: The hero's quest, the monster, the trickster, creation, the flood, betrayal, the lost paradise, the chosen one, the cursed line, the king's return and the haunted place. Every telling bends the legend toward the teller's values.

governs.title: Stories that move people
governs.text: A legend strengthens the one who fits it, shames a household or empties a place.

governs.title: Hero quests
governs.text: Questers enter a god's palace, the realm of the dead, a dream world or a holy place and face trials of skill, passion, faith and resolve. Rewards are blessings, items, rites, lifted curses, renewed lands, favours, true names and titles. A quester can succeed, fail, be trapped or be broken.

governs.title: Rewritten myths
governs.text: A quester who strays from the path may win a different reward, and the people's telling of the legend changes with the hero's return.

governs.title: Rites strengthened by myth
governs.text: Rites that re-enact a believed myth grow stronger, and stronger still at the myth's own site. A broken myth breeds a broken rite.

governs.title: Taboos (geis)
governs.text: Never refuse hospitality, never pass a burning house. A seer, a god or a rite lays the taboo at birth. A taboo can be a prohibition or a duty. Keeping it brings favour, breaking it brings disaster, and enemies set traps to make it break.

governs.title: True names
governs.text: Gods, spirits, some creatures, mortals and places have a true name. Knowing it lets you command or bind lesser beings. It is learned by deciphering old languages, through intrigue or from a teacher.

name: Clockwork Souls
intro: Clockwork Souls adds bodies that are made, not born, to the universe. Golems, automatons, homunculi and thinking war machines run on their own materials and power sources. They carry out their orders to the letter, so every order hides a loophole and every seal is a target for theft. When the maker dies, the made being goes on carrying out its last orders forever. Those that hold a bound soul inside slowly begin to want things.
outcome: Made beings bring the universe both powerful tools and unexpected stories.

governs.title: Made bodies
governs.text: Golems, automatons, homunculi and thinking war machines. Each has its material and a power source such as a bound soul, a rune, divine essence or a ley line.

governs.title: Orders to the letter
governs.text: Guard, serve, obey the holder of the seal, build, gather, destroy, report, maintain, replicate, hold still, follow and forbid. Orders hold always, while the maker lives, until a set date, when attacked or when a token is shown. Orders are given through an item, a word, a bloodline, an office or a network key. Every order hides a loophole.

governs.title: Fading runes
governs.text: Power sources run down, materials wear, and runes must be renewed by a skilled maker. Neglect breaks them.

governs.title: The maker's death
governs.text: When the maker dies, the made being carries out its last orders forever. It is a danger in every ruin and a guardian in every tomb.

governs.title: The soul in the machine
governs.text: Those that hold a bound soul inherit pieces of it and, over the epochs, begin to want things. Their will can grow from none to instructed, from emergent to full, and on to exceeding their maker.

governs.title: Legions from the foundry
governs.text: Identical beings made in great numbers from rare materials work the mines and fields and fill the ranks. They know no fear, but a dispel or a lost command seal stops them.

name: Forty Domains
intro: Forty Domains turns the gods' domains into working mechanics. Every domain does real work: salt curses the soil or keeps food from spoiling, glass grinds lenses for astronomers, lies twist rumours, the road protects travellers. Every domain splits into three or four aspects, so one war god can stand for courage and another for slaughter. Gods earn essence from activity in their domains, have goals and grudges, and build relationships of love, awe, fear or neglect with peoples.
outcome: Every god's domain is a real power you can feel across the universe.

governs.title: Mechanical domains
governs.text: From sea to fire, death to dream, war to craft, love to trickery, salt to sleep and technology to science, every domain does real work in the world.

governs.title: Aspects of domains
governs.text: Every domain splits into three or four aspects. Domains combine: a god of both the sea and death sends the drowned to an undersea realm.

governs.title: Forbidden pairings
governs.text: Aspects can be allied, neutral or mutually exclusive. Mercy and slaughter can never meet in the same god. Acts that drag a god toward a forbidden aspect cost it sanity.

governs.title: Essence earned through action
governs.text: Income depends on each domain's activity: battles for war, deaths for death, voyages for the sea. Gods feed their domains and compete for the same sailors.

governs.title: Gods with goals and grudges
governs.text: To be worshipped, to found a holy world, to destroy a rival, to spread their domain, to win a war, to acquire a relic, to raise a hero, to awaken a god, to defeat a foreign god, to make peace with the Creator or to rebel. Gods remember.

governs.title: Love, awe, fear and neglect
governs.text: Every people holds its own attitude toward every god. Answered prayers breed love, wrath breeds fear, silence breeds neglect, and neglect thins the faithful. Peoples worship a god out of devotion or to appease it.

governs.title: Hearts, schemes and wounds
governs.text: Gods feel anger, jealousy, pride and longing, and through their mortal agents they befriend, marry and slander one another. Their wounds come in kinds: a severed domain, a shattered body, a stolen true name or a void wound.
