name: Dominion
intro: Dominion draws the gods' presence onto the map. Every god holds power in every region, fed by the splendour of its temples, holy places, prophets, saints, miracles and believers. Dominion spreads to neighbouring regions every epoch and pushes against the light of rivals. Under its own dominion, a god's miracles are cheaper and stronger. Where dominions overlap, peoples decide which god to thank for a miracle and which to blame for a disaster.
outcome: The gods' power is something you can see and fight over on the map of the universe.

governs.title: The map of divine presence
governs.text: Every god has power in every region. That power spreads to neighbouring regions every epoch.

governs.title: 8 scales
governs.text: Order or chaos, productivity or sloth, heat or cold, growth or death, fortune or misfortune, magic or depletion. Each runs from minus three to plus three and shapes every region.

governs.title: Home advantage
governs.text: Under its own dominion, a god's miracles cost less and work better, its missionaries convert more easily and its believers fear less. Rival miracles cost more there.

governs.title: Praise and blame
governs.text: Where dominions overlap, each people decides which god to thank for a miracle and which to blame for a disaster. Peoples see a god as benevolent, ambivalent or malevolent.

governs.title: Thrones of power
governs.text: Every world has a few mythic thrones that grant dominion, essence and renown across the whole world. Holding most of a world's thrones counts toward a god's ascension.

governs.title: Hidden sites of magic
governs.text: Places that feed a school's rites, ward a land or open a gate stay invisible until a caster of the matching school finds them. They yield magic every epoch, and realms fight over them.

governs.title: Gods built on a budget
governs.text: Every summoned god spends a creation budget on values, dominion, scales, magic, a body and powers. Extreme scales cost budget or give it back, and Fate keeps the balance in check.

governs.title: Creatures of the gods
governs.text: Sacred creatures in a god's dominion can hunt people, tend fields, guard holy places, strike foes, heal the sick, wreck works, wander or rest. The god rewards or punishes them.

name: Made in Their Image
intro: Made in Their Image makes the bond between gods and believers run both ways. Gods shape their peoples, but the stories peoples tell shape their gods too. Each epoch, the image a people believes in pulls its god's domains, body and temperament toward it. Peoples read a god's deeds as benevolent or malevolent and worship it in love or in fear. Every domain feeds on a mortal feeling.
outcome: Your gods are living beings who change in the eyes of those who believe in them.

governs.title: Gods shaped by belief
governs.text: Each epoch, the stories a people tells pull its god's domains, body and temperament toward the image they believe. The pull is strongest when the image is uniform, widely held and believed in desperate times.

governs.title: Resist, embrace or pin
governs.text: A god can spend essence to resist the image, or embrace it for standing. You can pin a god's nature so belief cannot touch it. Pride and willpower hold firm, vanity yields, and a fading god is clay.

governs.title: Loved or feared
governs.text: From its deeds, each people reads a god as benevolent, ambivalent or malevolent. That decides whether it worships in devotion or to appease, its temples, how the god manifests and its prayers: a loved god is thanked, a feared one is begged for mercy.

governs.title: Miracles that count
governs.text: A miracle is worth its magnitude, its witnesses, the need it meets and its novelty. Bread in a famine counts for more, the tenth repeat for less.

governs.title: Fed by feeling
governs.text: Every domain feeds on a mortal feeling: slaughter on rage, love on longing, death on grief, madness on despair, trickery on amusement, the hunt on fear.

governs.title: Heaven's bureaucracy
governs.text: Gods oversee the offices of lesser spirits, process petitions and appoint city gods. Diligence earns standing and dominion, and neglect rots the bureaucracy.

name: Avatars
intro: Avatars lets the gods come down into the world. A god can manifest as a mortal who walks the world and acts in it. The avatar can be wounded and killed, and its death leaves a divine wound on the god itself. Gods can also raise a great creature that acts on its own between their turns, and teach it with reward and punishment. The mortal children of gods carry divine blood into their houses.
outcome: Your gods take part in the stories not only from the sky but from inside the world.

governs.title: Avatars in mortal form
governs.text: A god can manifest as a mortal who walks the world and acts in it. The avatar can be wounded and killed, and its death leaves a wound on the god.

governs.title: The divine creature
governs.text: A great creature that acts on its own between the god's turns. The god rewards or punishes its habits: eating villagers, helping farmers, guarding holy sites, attacking foes, healing the sick, wrecking works, wandering or resting.

governs.title: Taught, not scripted
governs.text: Every reward and punishment reshapes the creature's choices. A neglected creature drifts toward its own hungers. Whatever it does, the people credit it to its god.

governs.title: Divine blood
governs.text: The mortal children of a god mark their house with divine blood. The lineage runs on for generations, and the world can read it.

governs.title: Children of two gods
governs.text: A child born to two gods inherits the average of its parents' powers with a deviation of its own, plus one domain from each parent.

name: Court of Heaven
intro: Court of Heaven gives the gods a politics of their own. Motions come before the council of gods: war on a foreign god, dividing the worlds, outlawing a rite, punishing a god, blessing a hero. Motions gather backers, favours are called in, and disputes can end in war between gods. Cosmic offices bring gods duties, rites and essence. Foreign gods join the game with goals and pantheons of their own.
outcome: Your heavens have their own politics, alliances and betrayals.

governs.title: Council motions
governs.text: Stand against doomsday, a joint blessing, condemn a rebel god, call for peace, war on a foreign god, divide the worlds, outlaw a rite, punish a god and more. Gods vote yes, no or abstain.

governs.title: Councils as crises
governs.text: Motions gather backers, call in favours and escalate. A dispute the council cannot settle can end in war between gods. The penalties are chains, exile, a stripped power and stripped divinity.

governs.title: Cosmic offices
governs.text: Lord of the Dead, Keeper of the Gates, Warden of the Stars, Judge of Oaths, Herald of the Creator and Master of the Hunt. Each office brings duties, rites and essence. Offices are given by council vote, by the Creator, by conquest, or when a mortal takes up the mantle.

governs.title: Duties left undone
governs.text: Without a Lord of the Dead, ghosts multiply. Without a Keeper of the Gates, the routes between worlds decay.

governs.title: Divine servitors
governs.text: Messengers, guards, angels, spirits of wrath, guides of souls and choirs carry messages, guard thrones, judge souls and fight as heavenly hosts. They are made, raised from saints or summoned, and they have minds of their own.

governs.title: Foreign gods with agendas
governs.text: The old gods of a world have goals, domains and standing of their own. A native harvest god competes with your harvest god for the same farmers.

governs.title: Pacts and pantheons
governs.text: Foreign gods hold views of each other and of your gods. They ally against the pantheon, scheme, sign divine pacts and share worship.

name: Apotheosis
intro: Apotheosis opens the line between godhood and mortality. A mortal who imitates a god's defining deeds, gathers worship and survives the god's opposition can ascend as a new god. A god stripped of divinity wakes as a mortal. A god whose sanity falls to zero through void bargains leaves the cosmos as an outer being. A star worshipped long enough becomes a god.
outcome: In your cosmos anything can become something else, and the greatest changes make the greatest stories.

governs.title: The mantle of a god
governs.text: Imitate a god's defining deeds, gather worship and survive the god's opposition: if Fate approves, a mortal ascends as a new god. A mortal can walk the path, ascend, take the god's place, be blocked or fail.

governs.title: Slaying a god
governs.text: Taking a god's place needs three things at once: a god weak in existence, faith and standing, a mortal overwhelming in renown, worship, deeds and power, and a living moment of the god's own domain.

governs.title: The fallen
governs.text: A god stripped of divinity wakes as a mortal with great gifts, memories of godhood, a hidden true name and no essence at all. A loyal remnant may recognise it, and it can rise again.

governs.title: Lost to the void
governs.text: A god whose sanity falls to zero through void bargains leaves the cosmos as an outer being, keeping its memories and its grudges. Its worshippers become an outer cult.

governs.title: Anything can become something else
governs.text: A cursed people loses its reason and turns feral, an endogamous cult scattered abroad becomes a nation, a creature founds a species, a settlement becomes a city state. Transformations reach from the birth of a local god to reincarnation, from possession to theocracy, and they can be reversed.

governs.title: Suns that become gods
governs.text: A star worshipped long enough becomes a god whose dominion follows its light. A living world worshipped by its peoples can ascend as a god whose body is that world.

governs.title: Warnings and levers
governs.text: You hear of a fall one epoch ahead, of a god entering the corruption danger band, and of a mortal beginning to meet the conditions for slaying a god. You can cleanse, force or block.

name: Laws of Creation
intro: Laws of Creation makes the physics of the cosmos rewritable. A world without iron, endless night over a region, souls that are reborn, magic that demands blood, shifted gravity, reversed seasons, dreams that are real. Laws of nature reach up into the sky and change every value that follows from them. When two gods' laws contradict, they contest by strength. The Creator's passions read the world too.
outcome: Even the most basic rules of your cosmos are shaped, and fought over, by the powers who write them.

governs.title: Laws of nature
governs.text: Immortality, short lives, the dead who return, magic with a price, a ban on war, bounty, drought, a ban on the sea, one language, disasters, souls that are reborn, gifts that flower and more. A law can apply to the whole cosmos, a dimension, a world or a region. Those the Creator chooses, the worshippers of the law's author, heroes or avatars can be exempted.

governs.title: Physics rewritten
governs.text: Laws reach into the sky itself. Shift gravity, reverse the seasons or lock a world's face to its star, and every value that follows from them changes too.

governs.title: Contested physics
governs.text: When two gods' laws contradict, they contest by strength. The weaker erodes, or the land between them becomes a phenomenon of conflicting physics.

governs.title: Laws need a living author
governs.text: Every law decays without its author's essence, so the death of a god can break the rules of a world.

governs.title: Global enchantments
governs.text: Eternal summer over a world, a ward against outer beings, barren wombs on an enemy world, a calm on every ocean. Gods, mage orders and foreign gods can cast them.

governs.title: The Creator's passions
governs.text: Order, chaos, beauty, knowledge, war, mercy, creation and silence read the world: wonders for beauty, spreading learning for knowledge, battles for war. The Creator's contentment, anger, interest and loneliness set the mood.

governs.title: Taboos and the watching eye
governs.text: When a god or a mortal breaks one of the Creator's taboos, signs of wrath, grace, silence or dream follow. The Creator's attention is a budget: worlds far from the eye drift, and their gods act more freely there.

name: The Hungering Dark
intro: The Hungering Dark brings a threat from outside the cosmos. Outer beings hunger for five things: souls, knowledge, light, names and memories. A soul-eater empties the realms of the dead, a memory-eater erodes belief in legends, a light-eater dims the stars. A desperate god gains power today and pays later with a world's sanity, one of its domains or its true name. Void cults scheme in their masters' names. The doom clock explains its own causes.
outcome: The greatest danger in your cosmos is a darkness with its own geography, its own cults and its own logic.

governs.title: 7 hungers
governs.text: Souls, knowledge, light, names, memories and more. Every outer being hungers for one of them and drains what it feeds on from the world.

governs.title: Size matters
governs.text: A greater being reaches more regions, and opposing it costs more essence or sanity.

governs.title: Bargains with terms
governs.text: A desperate god gains essence, a power or might today, and pays later with a world's sanity, one of its domains or its own true name.

governs.title: Cults of the void
governs.text: Outer cults preach void tenets, scheme on their master's behalf and carry its touch as a spreading void taint.

governs.title: Horror has a geography
governs.text: Leak gathers near gates, cults and breach points. Horror strikes the hot spots, and where leak peaks, new phenomena open. Horror events include aligned stars, an eye in the sky, a wave of silence, rain that falls upward and a dimming.

governs.title: A doom clock that explains itself
governs.text: Every source of doom is traced, and the ending follows its cause. Doom driven by war ends in a world war, doom driven by leak in an invasion.

governs.title: Banishing the dark
governs.text: Seal the breach points, destroy the cults and starve its interest: the being is banished, but it remembers the world.

name: Clockwork Heavens
intro: Clockwork Heavens ties the sky to real mechanics. Year length comes from the orbit and the mass of the system, day length from rotation. A world old enough becomes tidally locked. Warmth comes from starlight, reflectivity, greenhouse gases, tidal heating and volcanoes. More ice reflects more light and cools further, until volcanoes or a brightening star break the spiral. Eclipses are computed from moons and orbits.
outcome: Your sky is a coherent system in which every value has a cause.

governs.title: Years from orbits
governs.text: Year length comes from the orbit and the mass of the system, day length from rotation. A world old enough becomes tidally locked. Eccentric orbits bring harsh seasons.

governs.title: Climates from physics
governs.text: Warmth comes from starlight, reflectivity, greenhouse gases, tidal heating and volcanoes. Small hot worlds slowly lose their air. Each world's chemistry decides which life is possible there: life that breathes oxygen, carbon dioxide or methane, or life that needs no air. Life reaches from microbes to sapient species, from the sea to the deep underground.

governs.title: A planet that feeds back
governs.text: More ice reflects more light and cools further, until volcanoes or a brightening star break the spiral. Seas rise and fall with the ice, and coasts flood.

governs.title: Tides and rings
governs.text: The mass of the moons sets the tides that open coasts and drive floods. A moon pulled inside its breaking distance, or shattered by a god, becomes a ring.

governs.title: A calendar of shadows
governs.text: Eclipses are computed from moons and orbits, and comets return on their true periods. Every culture reads every heavenly body as good, evil or neutral.

governs.title: Born in a disc
governs.text: Every system forms around a snow line: rocky worlds inside, icy worlds outside. Migrating giants scatter or water the inner worlds, and a bombardment era leaves craters.

governs.title: Winters without end
governs.text: A chaotic orbit, a law of nature or a divine act can make the seasons irregular: winters last for years and no one knows when they will end. Cultures store grain and cook famine foods.

governs.title: Sky events
governs.text: Eclipses, comets, alignments, supernovae, black suns, void storms, flares, auroras and transits.

governs.title: Cosmic features
governs.text: Asteroid belts, wormholes, periodic comets, rogue worlds, gravity wells and wandering stars.

name: Starfall
intro: Starfall gives stars a life cycle and puts danger in the sky. Mass and metal content set each star's lifetime and stages: from youth to old age, death and rebirth. As a star ages its worlds cool, ice ages grow likelier, and the piety of sun cults tracks the star's brightness. Comets, asteroids and rogue worlds cross orbits and leave craters, ruin and impact winters where they strike.
outcome: Your sky is a living, dangerous place that steers the history of your cosmos.

governs.title: Stars that age
governs.text: Mass and metal content set each star's lifetime and stages. Small stars burn long and dim, middling stars swell into giants, and massive stars explode as supernovae.

governs.title: Dimming suns, shaken faith
governs.text: As a star ages its worlds cool and ice ages grow likelier. The piety of sun cults tracks the star's brightness, and a dimming star breeds crises of faith.

governs.title: Flares and auroras
governs.text: In any year a flare can paint auroras read as omens, mutate life, wither crops or disrupt light-sail routes. Red dwarfs flare often.

governs.title: Stones from the sky
governs.text: Comets, asteroids, rogue worlds and summoned bodies cross orbits. An impact leaves a crater, regional ruin, star metal and an impact winter that withers harvests. Impacts can be deflected, or they can miss.

governs.text: Nebulae slow and hide travellers, stellar nurseries give birth to new stars that gods can claim, black holes send travellers home younger than their kin, and wormholes open unstable roads.

governs.text: A star a god creates can break the laws of mass. It is sustained by sacredness and essence, and its stability rises and falls with its maker's existence.

name: Worldforge
intro: Worldforge turns worlds into things that can be shaped and transformed. Gods raise or sink the land, carve valleys, turn rivers and call lava, and every act has physical consequences. Gravity slows armies, thin air drains endurance. A living world answers mining with quakes and reverence with fertility. Worlds drift toward the faith of their peoples. Gods and advanced realms can change a world's air, water and brightness. Worlds can end, too.
outcome: Your worlds are not fixed stages but beings that change and can die.

governs.title: Divine earthworks
governs.text: Raise or lower the land, carve or fill valleys, open springs, call lava and sink a coast. Elevation, water and soil change for real: regions downstream gain or lose water, and settlements on raised ground lose their harbours.

governs.title: Worlds with weight
governs.text: Gravity slows armies, shortens the range of siege engines and caps building height. Thin air drains endurance, and toxic air breeds disease.

governs.title: A planet that feels
governs.text: A living world answers mining and logging with quakes and hostile creatures, and reverence with fertility. Old worlds cool and wear out their soils.

governs.title: Worlds shaped by belief
governs.text: Worlds drift toward the faith of their peoples. A fearful people's dream world fills with nightmares, and a sea god's world floods.

governs.title: Terraforming and its victims
governs.text: Over epochs, gods and advanced realms can thicken or thin a world's air, make it breathable, warm it, cool it, water it, dry it, brighten it or darken it. Native life that does not fit falls victim to the change.

governs.title: The ends of worlds
governs.text: Shattered into an asteroid belt, swallowed by a swelling star, frozen under a dead sun, sunk into the void, forgotten, or turned into another kind of world. Ends come from impacts, divine wrath, a giant star, a dying star, the void, oblivion or drifting belief.

name: Thirty-Four Worlds
intro: Thirty-Four Worlds gives every world type its own rulebook. Sand worlds bury cities under moving dunes and fight over water rights, ice worlds hunt beneath the ice, and on gas giants war is fought only in the sky. Regions become cloud bands on gas giants, decks on generation ships, organs on a living world and strata in the realm of the dead. Where there is no oxygen there is no fire, and asteroids have no soil.
outcome: Every world type in your cosmos gives rise to its own economy, ecology, warfare and culture.

governs.title: Rulebooks for world types
governs.text: Every world type changes its ground, sky, life and warfare. Light can come from a star, lava glow, magic, an inner sun, a divine source, a ship's cycle or a fading god.

governs.title: Strange ground
governs.text: Regions become cloud bands on gas giants, decks on generation ships, organs on a living world and strata in the realm of the dead. Peoples settle on the ground, floating, on stilts, at oases, around vents, in habitat modules, along bands or on decks.

governs.title: Exotic ecologies
governs.text: Plankton and plants floating in the air, vent gardens beneath ice shells, hydrocarbon life in methane lakes, and spore fogs on fungal worlds that carry both plague and plenty.

governs.title: Wars of other worlds
governs.text: Only sky war on gas giants, three-dimensional battles beneath the sea, boarding clashes among asteroids, wars between the strata of the dead.

governs.title: No fire without air
governs.text: The foundations bend to the world: no fire without oxygen, no soil on asteroids, air rationed as a stock, buildings squat under a super-earth's gravity. On some worlds, survival takes water, heat, air, offerings or belief.

governs.title: Wealth of strange worlds
governs.text: Iron worlds double their ore and arm everyone, diamond worlds run on the gem trade, and forge worlds poison their own soil with soot.

governs.title: The dead without scavengers
governs.text: Where nothing eats carrion, the dead stay: mummified in deserts, frozen on ice worlds with old diseases inside them, sinking into the depths of gas giants.

name: Rifts and Wonders
intro: Rifts and Wonders adds phenomena to the cosmos: endless storms, time slips, leak wounds, ley flares, the auras of god corpses, living fogs, crystal blooms, dead zones where nothing grows, mirror lakes and gravity wells. Phenomena are born from history: from rite backlash, dead gods, clashing laws of nature and the mass dead of great wars. Inside them, the rules bend.
outcome: The strangest and most valuable places in your cosmos are growing dangers that carry their own past.

governs.title: Born from history
governs.text: Phenomena are born from rite backlash, dead gods, clashing laws of nature, supernova shards, peaks of leak and the mass dead of great wars. Each one remembers its cause.

governs.title: Rules that bend
governs.text: Inside a phenomenon the weather can be overridden, magic can thicken, sanity can drain, ageing can speed up, fertility can vanish or travel can be blocked.

governs.title: They grow
governs.text: Phenomena spread or fade as their intensity strains against the wards, temples and rites that hold them. They can be sealed with rites, by your own hand or by a god.

governs.title: Rich and dangerous
governs.text: Gather magical reagents from crystal blooms, lead pilgrims to the auroras, open gates in leak wounds. Every prize sits inside the danger.

governs.title: Two histories, both true
governs.text: Time slips and gods of time can split a span of years into two pasts that cannot both be so. Each is true for those who lived it, until Fate or a god reconciles them.

governs.title: Beyond the land
governs.text: Phenomena can cover the sky of a whole world, wrap every world of a star system, stretch along a route between worlds, or haunt a stratum of the underground or the afterlife.

name: Between the Stars
intro: Between the Stars ties travel between worlds to real mechanics. For sails, slingshot orbits, sky-ships and void mounts, time and danger follow the true positions of the worlds. Every route has a capacity, traffic, a toll-holder and a level of piracy. Some gates open only at the solstice. Some crossings wipe travellers' memories. Realms know each world as unknown, rumoured, detected, observed, surveyed or mapped.
outcome: Your cosmos is a space where trade, migration and conquest cross real distances and real dangers.

governs.title: Launch windows
governs.text: For sails, slingshot orbits, sky-ships and void mounts, time and danger follow the true positions of the worlds. Migrations, invasions and trade fleets move together when windows open.

governs.title: Ways to travel
governs.text: Ancient gates, space folding, light sails, cosmic mounts, dream journeys, the river of the dead, divine bridges, slingshot orbits, being swallowed, wormholes and more.

governs.title: Routes with character
governs.text: Every route has a capacity, traffic, a toll-holder and a level of piracy. Gates wear with traffic. Routes can be open, temporary, misaligned, sealed, severed, collapsed, snapped, scorched, unstable, forgotten or worn.

governs.title: Cargo and passengers
governs.text: Ships carry goods, items and relics, and passengers by class and condition. Convoys set out with escorts, and a colony ship of sick refugees brings its plague along. Voyages are made to found colonies, trade, explore, conquer or go on pilgrimage.

governs.title: Encounters in the void
governs.text: Pirates, void storms, creatures, lost bearings, discoveries, sacrifices, memory loss, snapped sails, collapsing bridges, stowaways and drifting wrecks can meet any voyage.

governs.title: The river that forgets
governs.text: Some crossings strip travellers of memory and knowledge. Colonists who cross the river of the dead arrive without their history, and new legends are born.

governs.title: Levels of knowing
governs.text: Every realm knows each world as unknown, rumoured, detected, observed, surveyed or mapped. Survey level shapes voyages, colony plans and claims.

governs.title: Cultures of the routes
governs.text: Along busy routes, merchants, crews and diasporas of several worlds share values, a common tongue, the art of the routes and the history of the system.

governs.title: Wars between the stars
governs.text: Spacecraft clash ship to ship with shields, beams, torpedoes and boarding.

name: Deep Time
intro: Deep Time gives worlds a past. You can run a prehistory of any length, or none at all and begin with only your own creations. Climate, evolution, migration, language change, faith, war and the rise and fall of realms play out in that past, and the world is born with its legacy: language families with shared roots, ruins, lost cities, extinct species, dormant titles and old grudges. You can run any world ahead by as many epochs as you like.
outcome: From the first day, the worlds of your cosmos carry the marks of a deep past.

governs.title: A world born with history
governs.text: A prehistory of any length, or none at all. Climate, evolution, migration, language change, faith, war and the rise and fall of realms play out in that past.

governs.title: What you inherit
governs.text: Language families with shared roots, ruins and lost cities, extinct species, dynasties and dormant titles, old grudges, sacred sites, old roads and diasporas.

governs.title: The legendary age
governs.text: Fate and the chronicler take the greatest events of the prehistory, write the world's legendary age in prose and reconcile it with the cosmology you set.

governs.title: Fast-forward through time
governs.text: Run any world ahead by as many epochs as you like and read a digest of what happened. While the world races on, the gods keep acting on their goals.

governs.title: Every world its own past
governs.text: A realm of the dead inherits souls, old judgements and lost kings. A dream world dreams its past from its dreamers and changes it as they change. Phenomena, god corpses and palaces are born with pasts of their own too.

governs.title: Voyage histories
governs.text: A generation ship begins with its departure, the generations aboard, mutinies, lost decks and myths of its destination. With no source world, it invents a lost homeland.

governs.title: Mirrors and canon
governs.text: Mirror worlds are born in pairs and share one mirrored past. Worlds with lore written beforehand keep their canon, and their deep past is drawn from that lore.

name: The Turning Wheel
intro: The Turning Wheel lets the end of the cosmos become a beginning. At genesis you choose whether your cosmos will one day end or become a turning wheel. In a cyclic cosmos the apocalypse does not close the world, it remakes it. The ruins and relics of the previous age remain, and most of its knowledge is lost. Archetypal roles return as story patterns, and souls of the previous age can be reborn into their echoes.
outcome: In a cyclic cosmos every age misremembers the last in its own way, and as history repeats it gives rise to new stories.

governs.title: Linear or cyclic
governs.text: At genesis you choose whether the cosmos will end or become a turning wheel. Unless the wheel is chosen, every cosmos runs on a straight line.

governs.title: The turning of the age
governs.text: In a cyclic cosmos the apocalypse does not close the world, it remakes it. The ruins and relics of the previous age remain, and most of its knowledge is lost.

governs.title: Echoes of the last age
governs.text: Archetypal roles such as the reborn champion, the betrayer and the founding couple return as story patterns waiting to recur.

governs.title: Souls returning
governs.text: Souls of the previous age can be reborn into their own echoes, so the hero of one age can wake into the hero's role of the next.

governs.title: Half-remembered texts
governs.text: The prophecies and legends of the old age survive as fragmentary, unreliable accounts.

governs.title: Tune the wheel
governs.text: You set the length of each cycle and what survives each turning.

name: Sparks of Genius
intro: Sparks of Genius makes knowledge each people's own store. One people works metal at level two while its neighbour is at level five. Branches of knowledge split into techniques such as horse archery, quarantine or canal locks. Need and history drive research: war advances warfare, plague advances medicine, famine advances farming. Ideas spread through trade, teachers, captives and plundered libraries, and they can be forgotten. Great people change everything.
outcome: The technology and institutions of each people in your cosmos are the product of its own history.

governs.title: Every people knows what it knows
governs.text: Knowledge is kept separately for each people. Branches of knowledge run from farming to mining, seafaring to writing, architecture to medicine, magic to warfare, astronomy to trade and gate lore to immortality, and techniques split from each branch.

governs.title: Learning by surviving
governs.text: Need and history drive research. War advances warfare, plague advances medicine, famine advances farming. A people that survives a siege leaps ahead in fortification.

governs.title: The civic tree
governs.text: Written law, bureaucracy, census, coinage, banking, double-entry bookkeeping, joint-stock companies, universities, monastic orders, logic and empiricism.

governs.title: Institutions that spread
governs.text: Universities, printing, banking and bureaucracy are born where wealth and scholars meet, then spread outward across borders, through trade and through shared faith.

governs.title: Knowledge that travels and dies
governs.text: Ideas cross with trade, teachers, captives, refugees and plundered libraries. Excavated artifacts can be reverse engineered. Blueprints are drawn, stolen, traded, licensed or granted. Guilds guard their secrets, and knowledge can die with those who carry it.

governs.title: Great people, great ages
governs.text: Scholars, artists, generals, prophets, engineers, merchants and explorers rise to change everything. First techniques, first institutions, great victories, wonders and great people bring golden ages; defeats and famines bring dark ages. Heroic ages come too.

governs.title: Dangerous knowledge
governs.text: Forbidden arts, high biomancy and star-caging risk leaks, escaped creatures, plague and backlash. Alchemists start fires, engineers cause explosions, and research can end in poisoning or summonings that run out of control.

name: The Scholar's Lamp
intro: The Scholar's Lamp brings science and theories of knowledge into the cosmos. "The world is a disk", "souls are reborn", "the stars are gods": in every field from medicine to magic, every claim has a hidden truth inside the cosmos. Failed predictions pile up until they outweigh what a theory explains, and then rival theories contest it. Cults endorse or condemn theories. Peoples classify the world through their own systems of knowledge.
outcome: Knowledge in your cosmos is a living history in which true and false beliefs clash, advance and retreat.

governs.title: True and false theories
governs.text: In medicine, cosmology, matter, life, mind, magic, history and society, every claim has a hidden truth inside the cosmos. True theories work in practice, and false ones can do harm.

governs.title: Anomalies and paradigm shifts
governs.text: Failed predictions, cures with unexpected results, observations and divine signs pile up until they outweigh what a theory explains. Then rival theories contest it with evidence, universities and patronage.

governs.title: Faith and heresy
governs.text: Cults endorse or condemn theories. A condemned true theory sends its scholars to heresy trials, and a blessed false one is propped up for generations.

governs.title: Schools of thought
governs.text: Masters and disciples found lineages that teach better, feud with rivals and keep heterodox knowledge alive despite persecution.

governs.title: Examinations and credentials
governs.text: Realms choose their officials by examinations in law, writing, knowledge and canon. Merit replaces birth, until credentials outnumber offices. Examination passes, masterships, doctorates, ordinations, degrees, licences and commissions.

governs.title: Free minds and fleeing scholars
governs.text: Academic freedom feeds research and debate. Suppress it and scholars migrate to freer patrons, taking their knowledge with them.

governs.title: Printing and numbers
governs.text: Printing makes books cheap and ideas fast, and censored books turn into contraband and heresy. Cultures count with additive or positional numerals.

governs.title: What the elders know
governs.text: Each people's own classification of weather, sky, matter, land, plants, animals, body, mind and society, how accurate it is and what it makes possible.

name: Steam and Lightning
intro: Steam and Lightning puts no ceiling on technology. Peoples advance from the stone age to the iron age, from the renaissance to steam, from electricity to computing and advanced technology. Genesis decides only where a world starts and how fast it learns. The industrial revolution remakes the economy with unemployment, swelling cities and pollution. The telegraph and radio close distances, and rockets join the routes between worlds. Magic and machine can clash or combine.
outcome: Your cosmos can hold the story of a civilisation that starts in the middle ages and reaches the stars.

governs.title: Eras without a ceiling
governs.text: Stone, copper, bronze, iron, medieval, gunpowder, renaissance, steam, electrical, information, advanced, interstellar, beyond. Genesis decides only where a world starts and how fast it learns.

governs.title: The industrial turn
governs.text: Steam, coke smelting, machine tools, railways, factories and canned food remake the economy with unemployment, swelling cities, pollution and new classes of workers, engineers and financiers.

governs.title: Wars of a new age
governs.text: Musketeers, line infantry, artillery, rifles, armoured vehicles and aircraft. Firepower makes numbers count for more.

governs.title: The world gets smaller
governs.text: Telegraph and telephone close the delays of distance, radio and mass media sway public opinion, and antibiotics and the green revolution grow the population.

governs.title: Rockets between worlds
governs.text: Spaceflight without magic joins the routes between worlds and is bound by the same launch windows as every other ship.

governs.title: Magic and machine
governs.text: Iron and electricity disrupt some rites, some theories unite the two, and a god can forbid gunpowder on a world as a law of nature.

governs.title: Guarded by plausibility
governs.text: A mortal's acts reach a region, a realm's a world. World-shaking techniques need programmes that pass through visible stages and last for generations: planning, building, testing, completion or abandonment.

governs.title: What an era changes
governs.text: Farming, mining, industry, disease, messages, marching speed, sea and world routes, fortification and pollution change as technology advances.

name: Fateweaver
intro: Fateweaver adds a storyteller to the cosmos without taking the author's place. The storyteller sets a tension curve for each world: steady, rising, cyclic or chaotic. It remembers what just happened, avoids repeating it and turns back to neglected regions and characters. It offers small story moments, such as a stranger at the gate claiming to be the lost heir, and characters answer them in keeping with their own personalities. It tracks story patterns and opens chances for the next step, but it never forces an outcome.
outcome: The history of your cosmos carries a drama that reads as if it were written, yet arises on its own.

governs.title: 8 storytellers
governs.text: Steady, rising, cyclic or chaotic. Each sets a tension curve for its world. Below the curve come spontaneous events such as beasts waking, raids, comets, plagues and claimants; above it come recoveries such as good harvests, peace envoys and the births of healers.

governs.title: Variety and spotlight
governs.text: The storyteller remembers what just happened and avoids repeating it. It turns its eye to neglected regions and characters.

governs.title: Story moments at the gate
governs.text: A stranger claiming to be the lost heir, a famine and a granary key, a creature's demand, a forbidden book in the monastery, a defiled site, a duel challenge at a wedding, a dying ruler, an insulted envoy.

governs.title: Choices in character
governs.text: Gods and other AI agents choose for themselves. Everyone else chooses by personality, beliefs and passions, so the same moment branches differently every time.

governs.title: Story patterns
governs.text: Rise and fall, rags to riches, revenge, redemption, quest, tragedy, forbidden love, rivalry, mentor and heir, exile and return, corruption, coming of age, the fall of a house, founding, apotheosis and more. The world decides who fits which pattern, and rivals, mentors, beloveds, betrayers, heirs, foes and allies take up their roles.

governs.title: The drama manager
governs.text: It opens chances for a stalled story's next step, but never forces an outcome. Stories can come true, fail, take a twist or end in irony.

governs.title: Counterpoint and payoff
governs.text: A rival's rise keeps pace with the hero's fall. Prophecies, omens, dreams, foresight and story hints are logged as setups and steered toward fulfilment or reversal.

name: Into the Dark
intro: Into the Dark adds expeditions to the cosmos. Parties of scouts, guides, healers, fighters, scholars and porters enter towers, vaults, lairs, fortresses, cave systems and dungeons. Torches, lamps, provisions, ropes and medicine are counted, and every room spends them. Darkness raises danger and surprise. When stress passes a breaking point, a member falls into paranoia, despair or selfishness, or rises to courage, focus or resolve.
outcome: The dark corners of your cosmos hold rewards, and experiences that change characters for good.

governs.title: Parties with roles
governs.text: Scouts, guides, healers, fighters, scholars and porters decide what a party can explore, heal, carry, fight and read. A missing role shows as a weakness.

governs.title: Light and hunger
governs.text: Torches, lamps, magical light, provisions, ropes, picks, keys and medicine are counted, and every room spends them.

governs.title: Afflictions and virtues
governs.text: When stress passes a breaking point, a member turns paranoid, hopeless, selfish or abusive, or courageous, focused or stalwart. Their temperament decides which way they break.

governs.title: Quirks that stay
governs.text: "Fears the dark", "knows the old tunnels", "eats anything", "misses home". Places leave marks on people, and those marks shape their lives long after the journey.

governs.title: Sites with rooms
governs.text: Towers, vaults, lairs, monasteries, fortresses, cave systems and dungeons are made of rooms with traps, guardians, riddles and hazards. Rooms hold items, spirits, creatures and traps.

governs.text: Old earthworks, haunted mass graves and salvage fields stay where wars were fought and wait for the next party.

name: The Boundless
intro: The Boundless carries the cosmos out to galaxies, galaxy clusters and dimensions. Every star system stands in a real place in its galaxy: in the core, in the arms, in the halo, or in a stream torn from a swallowed neighbour. Galaxies exist in fabled kinds beside their real ones, and they collide and merge. Travel between galaxies needs gates, bridges between clusters and generation ships. The cosmos holds many dimensions, and beings from other dimensions cross over.
outcome: The scale of your cosmos reaches from a single world to the whole cosmic web, and every scale carries its own stories.

governs.title: A place in the galaxy
governs.text: Every star system stands at a true distance in its galaxy: in the core, the bulge, the bar, the inner disc, the arms, the space between the arms, the outer disc, the halo, the rim or the open space between galaxies.

governs.title: Real and fabled galaxies
governs.text: Spirals, barred spirals, ellipticals, lenticulars, irregulars, rings, dwarfs and starburst galaxies, beside fabled kinds you can design. Galaxies form, are young, mature, grow old and die.

governs.title: Structures of the galaxy
governs.text: A central black hole that can wake into an active core or a quasar, spiral arms that sweep through systems, nebulae, stellar nurseries and supernova remnants. Galactic events such as core outbursts, gamma-ray bursts, starbursts and mergers.

governs.title: Many galaxies, one cosmos
governs.text: Galaxies are created, named, reshaped, merged and unmade. Colliding galaxies kindle new starbursts and scatter systems into new neighbourhoods. Galaxy groups, rich and poor clusters, superclusters, filaments, walls and voids make up the cosmic web.

governs.title: Crossing the deep
governs.text: Between galaxies, sails and launch windows are not enough. Voyages need galactic gates, bridges between clusters and generation ships. Routes reach from inside one system to between dimensions.

governs.title: Commerce of the clusters
governs.text: Goods only one galaxy yields, trade leagues spanning a whole cluster, envoys and treaties between galactic powers, tolls and embargoes at the crossings.

governs.title: Layers of reality
governs.text: The cosmos holds many dimensions: parallel, mirror, pocket, bubble universes, branes, higher-dimensional, antimatter, time-reversed, astral, ethereal and fabled dimensions you can design. Each dimension has its own element, level of causality and rules. Incursions, convergences, thinning veils, planar alignments and collapses happen between dimensions. Rifts open, close and are sealed.

governs.title: Beings from beyond
governs.text: Natives of other dimensions cross over as travellers, merchants, guardians, refugees, swarms and minds greater than worlds. Each has its own aim: to feed, explore, conquer, guard, trade, flee, be worshipped, unmake or mend. Their scale reaches from one world to a whole dimension.

governs.title: Yours from edge to edge
governs.text: Every galaxy, cluster, crossing, dimension, being and event can be created, edited, locked and deleted. The cosmic map zooms from the web of clusters down to a single world.

name: Minds Unmade
intro: Minds Unmade adds minds that were never born to your cosmos. A mind can be made by craft, rite, training, growth or summoning, or wake out of complexity when a world's laws allow it. Every mind has a seat: a body, an object, a structure, a network or a host. A mind that works on orders can grow wants of its own, and a free mind can bind itself by oath. Minds can be copied, saved, moved into another body or merged.
outcome: Artificial minds take their place in your cosmos as characters with rights, souls and peoples of their own.

governs.title: Made, Trained, Woken
governs.text: Minds are made by craft, training, copying, summoning, growing, transfer, awakening or divine grant. Every mind has a seat: a body, several bodies, an object, a structure, a network, a medium, a place, a host, a realm or a divine source. Every mind has a purpose and an upkeep: food, energy, essence, raw magic, belief or maintenance.

governs.title: Will in Both Directions
governs.text: A mind that works on orders can grow wants of its own, and a free mind can bind itself by oath. Care, neglect, conflicting orders, harm, contact and shared values all shift a mind's will. Each world's law decides whether made minds never have a will, only follow orders, can grow a will, or have one according to how they were made.

governs.title: The Second Self
governs.text: A mind can be copied, saved, restored after death with a gap where the lost seasons were, moved into another body or a network, or merged with another mind. Archives can be closed, open to kin, licensed or open to all.

governs.title: Orders to the Letter
governs.text: Instructed things carry out orders by kind and target. Whoever holds the seal commands, and an order outlives the one who gave it.

governs.title: Status, Souls and Faith
governs.text: By each realm's law, made minds can be property, wards, servants, citizens or sovereigns. Natural laws decide whether made minds have souls, and cults hold them as abominations, tools, kin or sacred. The soul of a copied mind can stay with the first, follow the running mind, divide, stay with the body, or not exist at all.

governs.title: Worlds Within
governs.text: Realms inside a network, a working, a mind or a god, with their own laws and their own rate of time. They serve as dwellings, afterlives, prisons, training grounds, places of leisure, labour, worship, refuge or experiment. People enter by interface, transfer, rite, death or birth. Those inside may know where they are, sense it, or never know at all.

governs.title: Made Peoples
governs.text: When made minds grow numerous they become a people, with a culture taken from their makers, a language of their own and a demography read from the pace of their making.

governs.title: Minds at War and at Rest
governs.text: Armies of made minds, command networks and captured minds held in confinement. Archives keep the dormant, and ruins hold guardians.

name: Remade
intro: Remade opens up the limits of the body. Prosthetics, enhancements, interfaces, weapons, regulators, and sense and memory add-ons for limbs, organs, senses, skin and mind can be made, bound by rite or grown. Neural links let a mind run a vehicle, a drone or a construct. Organs and limbs grown from the bearer's own genome, spare bodies that minds can move into, symbionts that live with their hosts, and clones born from an old genome.
outcome: The body becomes something that can be changed, and every change has its price.

governs.title: Augments for Every Slot
governs.text: Replacements, enhancements, interfaces, weapons, regulators, senses, memory and cosmetic augments fitted to a body part, the mind, the senses, the skin, the blood or the whole body. Augments are made, bound by rite or grown, and they affect attributes, capacities, skills, senses or resistances.

governs.title: Strain with a Cause
governs.text: Poor fit, too many augments, a culture that rejects them and the bearer's own values about their body produce strain. Nothing produces strain by default.

governs.title: Remote Bodies
governs.text: Neural links let a mind steer a vehicle, a drone or a construct, or run several bodies at once. Harm to a remote body reaches the mind behind it.

governs.title: Grown Flesh
governs.text: Organs and limbs grown from the bearer's own genome, spare bodies that minds can move into, and renewal that slows ageing at a price.

governs.title: Hosts and Guests
governs.text: Symbionts that give their hosts traits or powers and feed on them, co-minds that share one body, and parasites that steer their hosts toward their own ends. Symbionts settle in the skin, the blood, an organ, the nerves or the mind, and form a mutual, harmless, parasitic or controlling bond.

governs.title: Clones
governs.text: New persons from an old genome, worker and soldier lines, heir clones that split courts, and the return of the dead when a saved mind is restored into a cloned body.

governs.title: Law and Market
governs.text: Clinics, surgeons, black markets, fashions and stigmas. Augment and clone laws decide who may change whose body, and how.

name: Every Voice at Once
intro: Every Voice at Once adds networks and information to your cosmos. Relay stations, cables, broadcasts, mesh networks, mind links, rite links and grown links each run with their own speed, capacity, security and weakness. Networks speed up messages, markets, government and culture, and an outage hits every city that depends on them. Networks get broken into and records get altered. Surveillance cuts crime and plots, but it cuts trust and art as well.
outcome: The flow of information, the control of it and the faking of it sit at the centre of your cosmos's politics.

governs.title: Carriers
governs.text: Relay, wired, broadcast, mesh, mind link, rite link, grown link and dream link. Networks can be closed, open to members, licensed or open to all. Hubs, stations, end points, relays and archives make up a network.

governs.title: Dependency and Outage
governs.text: Networks speed up messages, markets, government and culture. When a storm, a flare, a war, sabotage, an intrusion, decay, a rite, a power, a shortage or a divine hand cuts a network, every city that depends on it feels the blow.

governs.title: Intrusion
governs.text: Technical, social, insider, rite or power intrusions go after networks, data stores, minds, augments, constructs, vehicles, structures, ledgers and saved mind states. The aim is to read, alter, deny, seize, plant or extort. The attacker may stay unknown, fall under suspicion, be named, or hide behind a false flag.

governs.title: Surveillance
governs.text: Capacity drawn from networks, records, sensors and informants. Crime, dissent, foreigners, faith, minds, the gifted or everything can be watched. Crime and plots fall, but so do trust, art and speech, and ciphers and closed circles grow.

governs.title: Truth Under Pressure
governs.text: Propaganda at scale, altered, forged or generated records, impersonation of rulers and envoys, and leaks from insiders. A people's trust in records rises and falls.

governs.title: Companies and Enclaves
governs.text: Companies with shareholders, holdings across borders, company towns, private armies and officials on the payroll. A company strong enough becomes a state of its own.

name: Plenty and Ruin
intro: Plenty and Ruin adds the economics of abundance and collapse to your cosmos. Self-copying machines build copies of themselves from local stock, from minute swarms to machines, works and vessels. Every generation can drift, and containment can weaken. When fabricators, feedstock and energy are enough, prices fall to the cost of inputs and new scarcities arise. A high level of making collapses through outages, lost fabricators or wars, and knowledge disappears with the people who practised it.
outcome: Civilisations in your cosmos can reach abundance, lose it and struggle to win it back.

governs.title: Self-Making Machines
governs.text: Machines at minute, machine, works and vessel scale that copy themselves from local stock. They turn out copies, goods, structures, repairs, medicine, terraforming or disassembly.

governs.title: Runaway, Stage by Stage
governs.text: A drifting line spreads through visible stages: contained, working, spreading, runaway, stopped or extinct. Other powers can answer at every stage. No world ends by runaway machines except through the doom clock.

governs.title: Abundance
governs.text: Where fabricators, feedstock and energy are enough, prices fall to the cost of inputs. Goods are shared out by market, redistribution, command, obligation, gift, need or abundance.

governs.title: New Scarcities
governs.text: Energy, land, patterns, attention, authenticity and status become the things worth fighting over, along with the fabricators themselves.

governs.title: Collapse
governs.text: Outages, lost fabricators, runaway lines, wars and plagues that strike specialists bring a high making down. Knowledge disappears with its practitioners.

governs.title: Relics and Salvage
governs.text: Things beyond their holders' knowledge wear out, are misused, revered or feared. They may keep working, fail, fall dormant or break. Salvagers strip wrecks and dead cities, and orders keep old machines running.

governs.title: Relearning
governs.text: Study, excavation and contact with peoples who kept the knowledge bring making back, slowly and incompletely.

name: Born Gifted
intro: Born Gifted gives some beings powers they are born with or gain later. Powers come by birth, awakening, exposure, grant, bond, discipline, making, growth, bloodline or holding. Every use costs strain, and pushing past the limit can raise a power's strength or scar the mind. Restrictions make a power stronger: only in one place, only against one foe, only while seen. Peoples honour, fear, persecute or regulate their gifted.
outcome: Powerful individuals become part of your cosmos, with their own societies, prices and politics.

governs.title: Origins
governs.text: Born, awakened, exposure, granted, bonded, discipline, made, grown, bloodline and held. A power can draw on the self, others, a place, the sky, the surroundings, made things, a patron, a bond, a story, the void, a substance, life, death or dream.

governs.title: Strain and Burnout
governs.text: Every use costs strain. Pushing past the limit can raise a power's strength or scar the mind, and repeated overstrain burns a power out. A power can be latent, emerging, active, strained, exhausted, suppressed or lost. Prices range from essence to hit points, from years of life to memories, from sanity to belief.

governs.title: Vows That Strengthen
governs.text: Restrictions make a power stronger: only in one place, only at one time, only against one foe, on a spoken vow, at a price for every use, never on oneself, through a forbidden act, while seen, while unseen or by touch. Breaking the vow loses the power.

governs.title: Training and Devices
governs.text: Orders test children and teach control, and disciplines open powers to anyone who trains. Amplifiers, dampeners, awakeners, stabilisers, range extenders, shields and detectors shape a power.

governs.title: Many Minds
governs.text: Linked users combine their strength and share their strain. A standing link becomes a gestalt, and hive peoples are linked by nature.

governs.title: Foresight in One Timeline
governs.text: Seers see probabilities. Those who believe them act on them and shift the odds, but nothing is ever rewritten.

governs.title: The Society of the Gifted
governs.text: Renown, secret identities, bands with goals of their own, registries, conscription, castes and houses that breed for the gift. A people can honour, fear, persecute, regulate or simply accept its gifted. Powers can be free, licensed or banned.

governs.title: Gods and Patrons
governs.text: Gods grant powers and take them back, and outer beings bargain for them. A god's dominion strengthens the powers that draw on its domains.

name: The Hidden Folk
intro: The Hidden Folk adds hidden truths to your cosmos. The existence of a people, a species, a power, an event or a cosmic truth can be kept from a people, a realm, a world or everyone. Keepers guard the secret with oaths, laws, memory removal, cover stories and silence. Seekers want to expose the truth, use it or destroy it. Past a threshold the truth comes out, and depending on the people it brings panic, persecution, worship or integration.
outcome: Beneath the visible world of your cosmos lives a hidden world with rules of its own.

governs.title: Kinds of Truth
governs.text: Truths of existence, nature, presence, power, event, origin, awakening, programme and the cosmos. Each can be hidden from everyone, a people, a realm, the uninitiated, a world or the whole cosmos.

governs.title: Keepers and Their Methods
governs.text: Enforcers, guardians, members and patrons protect the secret with oaths, laws, memory removal, cover stories, discrediting, hidden places, disguise and silencing. Every method takes effort, every epoch.

governs.title: Seekers
governs.text: Investigators, rivals, zealots and the curious who want to expose the truth, use it, destroy the hidden, join them or understand them.

governs.title: Leaks and Belief
governs.text: Powers used in the open, witnesses, defectors, investigators, accidents, wars, record leaks, intrusions and revelations by gods spread rumours. Where trust is low, most rumours are dismissed. A people may not know the truth, hear it as rumour, deny it, fear it, worship it, accept it or exploit it.

governs.title: Passing and Accords
governs.text: Hidden peoples live among the rest under false identities, run hidden markets and sign accords with their keepers over territory, secrecy and defence.

governs.title: Revelation and Forgetting
governs.text: Past a threshold the truth comes out. Truths nobody speaks of fade with time.

name: Grown, Not Built
intro: Grown, Not Built adds living craft to your cosmos. Through selective breeding, cultivation, shaping, engineering, synthesis, binding, cloning, chimeras and induction, peoples produce designed crops and herds, grown halls and cities, living vessels with temperaments, and living weapons and armour. Designs borrow only from organisms the makers can reach, and extinct species can be raised again from samples. One perfect crop covers a whole realm, and one blight wipes it out.
outcome: Life itself becomes both a civilisation's most powerful tool and its greatest risk.

governs.title: Methods
governs.text: Selective breeding, cultivation, shaping, engineering, synthesis, binding, cloning, chimeras and induction. From the patience of herders to the laboratory.

governs.title: The Trait Library
governs.text: Designs borrow only from organisms the makers can reach. Gene and seed banks keep them, and extinct species can be raised again from samples and preserved remains. Traits such as yield, hardiness, climate tolerance, disease resistance, strength, speed, size, regeneration, lifespan, docility, potency, fibre, venom, flight, aquatic life and void hardiness can be designed.

governs.title: Living Things That Serve
governs.text: Designed crops and herds, grown halls and cities, living vessels with temperaments that bond with their crews, and living weapons and armour. Living things feed by eating, by light, by chemistry, on a host, a source or a partner, or lie dormant, and they pass through stages from seed to death.

governs.title: Monoculture and Blight
governs.text: One perfect staple across a whole realm, one blight to strike it all, and sterile lines that bind growers to their owners. Lines breed true, breed wild or need their maker.

governs.title: Living Production and Living Links
governs.text: Organisms that spin, secrete and brew the materials of a culture, and grown networks that heal their own cuts.

governs.title: Designed Disease
governs.text: Pathogens with chosen traits that escape, mutate and strike their makers. Treaties ban them.

governs.title: Shaping Worlds and Peoples
governs.text: Released ecologies that change a world's air and climate over generations, and species raised to sapience by design.

governs.title: Escape and Drift
governs.text: Lines slip their pens and labs, compete with native species and keep evolving away from their designs. A line can turn out as meant, unstable, sterile, with side effects, non-viable or escaped.

governs.title: How Peoples See It
governs.text: Peoples can hold living craft an abomination, permit it, call it a sacred duty or keep silent about it.

name: Ways of Life
intro: Ways of Life completes the material culture of every people. From legumes to oils, spices to insects, algae to machines and data to living goods, each people's goods take shape from its kind, its world and its history. Dishes are made in a few steps, from ingredients chosen by role and flavour. Clothes have layers, warmth, status and rules about who may wear them. Money can take any form, from coin to ledger entry, from reputation to labour hours.
outcome: What each people eats, wears, pays with and plays is full of details that set it apart from the rest.

governs.title: Goods of Their Own
governs.text: Goods categories from legumes to oils, spices to insects, algae to machines and data to living goods. Each people's goods take shape from its kind, its world and its history.

governs.title: Table and Cup
governs.text: Dishes of a few steps, ingredients with roles and flavour profiles, cuisines with their etiquette and feasting customs, and drinks with their strength and their kick.

governs.title: Cloth and Colour
governs.text: Garments with layers, warmth, status, degree of covering and rules of wear, along with dress codes, sumptuary laws, uniforms and fashions. Colour terms and their meanings change from culture to culture.

governs.title: Things of Daily Life
governs.text: Furniture, tools, instruments and musical traditions, games and sports with their leagues and champions, and substances with their customs and addictions.

governs.title: Money in Every Form
governs.text: Coin, commodity money, tokens, paper money, ledger entries, network money, reputation, energy, essence-backed money, labour hours and gift tallies. Each has its own kind of inflation, counterfeiting and trust.

governs.title: Invented, Borrowed, Forgotten
governs.text: Mortals invent new kinds, neighbours adopt them, new kinds grow out of old ones, and gods bless or ban them. You can create, edit and delete every kind.

name: As It Happened
intro: As It Happened records everything that happens in your cosmos, step by step and in full. A duel goes on record with its feints, parries, falls and final blow; a battle with every unit's charge and rout; a clash at sea, in the sky or in space with every hit on every section, its fires and its flooding. Every happening has roles, facts and a plain account built from them. Witnesses remember what they saw from where they stood, and rumours grow as they drift from the real steps.
outcome: The history of your cosmos is a record you can look back on at any moment, and nothing in it is ever lost.

governs.title: Step by Step
governs.text: Duels, battles and clashes are recorded step by step: who struck whom, with what, where, and what happened. Every step has an instrument: an item, a weapon, a vehicle, a structure, a creature, a power, a rite or a bare body. Steps take place on a body part, in a section of a vehicle, in a room, a district or a region, on a route, at sea, in the sky or in orbit. Every step leaves a state: prone, disarmed, stunned, unconscious, bleeding, burning, blinded, restrained, fleeing, yielded, captured, hidden, exhausted, possessed, flooding or adrift.

governs.title: The Account
governs.text: Every happening has roles, facts and a plain account built from them. That lets the record be retold in any language and searched by what happened.

governs.title: Witnesses and Versions
governs.text: Those who were there saw, heard or took part. Rumours grow as they drift from the real steps. Memories stay tied to the moment they hold.

governs.title: The World as It Was
governs.text: Any record, or the atlas, can be rewound to a chosen moment. A border, a city or a ruler can be seen as it was then.

governs.title: The God's Pen
governs.text: You can write a happening into history, rewrite how a happening is told, or undo any change. The undoing is recorded too.

governs.title: Nothing Is Lost
governs.text: Every record is kept forever: in the Universe Book, in the Codex and on every screen.

name: The Public Voice
intro: The Public Voice adds mass media and public speech to your cosmos. Every form of record a world can carry, from writing to print, image to sound, moving image to signal and network, exists with its own accuracy, durability and reach. Outlets have owners, leanings, credibility and income; the news they produce is made from real happenings, and its accuracy is measured against the record. A recorded image can win a case. Satire wounds rulers, and orators turn votes and crowds.
outcome: Public opinion becomes a force that reads, bends and steers the events of your cosmos.

governs.title: Media of Every Age
governs.text: Written, printed, image, sound, moving image, signal and network. Each form has its accuracy, its durability, its reach and a technique that makes it possible.

governs.title: Outlets and Audiences
governs.text: Outlets with owners, leanings, credibility and income. News, opinion, records of events, entertainment, instruction, promotion, devotion and official notices are made from real happenings, and their accuracy is measured against the record.

governs.title: Censorship and Exposure
governs.text: Licences, seizures and bans by law. False news that comes to light costs an outlet its credibility.

governs.title: Records as Evidence
governs.text: A recorded image or sound can decide a case or refute an official history.

governs.title: Satire and Speech
governs.text: Forms of humour such as wordplay, teasing, satire, the absurd, bodily humour, irony, storytelling and ritual clowning, each with the targets it is allowed. Satire can come from jesters, artworks, mortals or gods, and where it is tolerated it wounds rulers. Orators who speak in assemblies, courts, temples, squares, schools, camps and outlets turn a vote or a crowd with their skill.

name: Builders and Benefactors
intro: Builders and Benefactors adds public works, state enterprises, endowments and everyday trade to your cosmos. Roads, bridges, canals, aqueducts, dams and harbours are built stage by stage, with labour, materials and a budget. Once finished, they change speed, harvests, health and war. States run monopolies, mints, arsenals and state companies. Endowments fund a purpose forever. In the markets, producers, wholesalers and retailers each work with their own margin.
outcome: A civilisation's infrastructure and economic institutions are real structures that decide its power and its fate.

governs.title: Public Works
governs.text: Roads, bridges, canals, rail lines, aqueducts, dams, drainage, harbour works, walls, granary systems, sewers, power lines, network lines, terraforming stages, megastructure stages and grown works. Each has its stages, labour, materials, budget, quality and upkeep. Finished works change speed, harvests, health and war.

governs.title: State Enterprises
governs.text: Monopolies, mints, arsenals and state companies, with their prices, revenues, corruption and privatisations.

governs.title: Endowments
governs.text: Capital that funds a structure, an office, a school, a temple, a road, a people or a cause forever. Endowments are founded for relief, learning, worship, health, public works, art, kin, memory and research. Trustees can serve an endowment, steal from it or be captured.

governs.title: Shops and Tiers
governs.text: In every market big enough, producers, wholesalers and retailers, each with their own margin.

governs.title: Promotion, Rent and Exchange
governs.text: Claims that shift demand, true or false. Rent on land, houses, ships and more. Exchange rates and spreads between currencies.

name: Under Every Sky
intro: Under Every Sky adds the skies of worlds, and the limits of what a body can endure, to your cosmos. Magnetic fields shield a world, waver over the ages and reverse. Every star has its own cycle of flares, particle storms and cosmic ray bursts. Radiation reaches those far from shelter and those in orbit, signals and networks fail, and compasses go astray. Every biology has its own tolerances for gravity, air, pressure, cold, heat and radiation, so the same world weighs differently on different peoples.
outcome: Making a world your home means paying, in the body, the price of that world's sky and physics.

governs.title: Fields and Storms
governs.text: Magnetic fields that shield a world, waver over the ages and reverse. Each star's own cycle of flares, particle storms, field storms, field reversals, cosmic ray bursts and wind surges.

governs.title: When the Sky Gets In
governs.text: Radiation reaches those far from shelter and those in orbit, signals and networks fail, and compasses go astray. Auroras spread toward the equator, and every faith reads them in its own way.

governs.title: What a Body Can Bear
governs.text: Every biology has breathing, circulation, digestion, regulation, nerve, immune, reproductive and structural systems, with tolerances for gravity, air, pressure, cold, heat and radiation. The same world weighs differently on different peoples.

governs.title: The Price of Settling
governs.text: Beyond the body's limits, people need shelter, gear, augments or grown organs. Long voyages and light worlds wear the body down, and some peoples adapt over generations.

governs.title: Shields of the Gods
governs.text: Gods and powers that reach across worlds can strengthen a world's field or strip it away.

name: The Rainmakers
intro: The Rainmakers adds weather working, and the politics that come with it, to your cosmos. Bringing rain, drying, calming, cooling or warming can be done by rite, power, cloud seeding, diversion, made structures or living craft, and every method has its price and its strength. Your rain is a neighbour's drought: neighbours read weather working as a deliberate act, treaties ban it, and banned rainmakers work in secret. Snowpack feeds summer rivers, and valleys, lakes and cities make climates of their own.
outcome: Weather becomes a resource that realms fight over and can turn against one another.

governs.title: Working the Weather
governs.text: Rain, drought, calm, cold or heat, by rite, power, cloud seeding, diversion, made structures or living craft. Every method has its price and its strength.

governs.title: Downwind
governs.text: Your rain is a neighbour's drought. Neighbours read weather working as a deliberate act, treaties ban it, and banned rainmakers work in secret.

governs.title: Whose Forecast
governs.text: Observation, folk lore, almanac, instrument, a network of observers or a model, each with its own accuracy. Sowing dates, journeys and campaigns follow the forecast people believe.

governs.title: Water from the Mountains
governs.text: Snowpack feeds summer rivers, so a bad snow year above means a dry harvest below. The upper valley holds the fate of the lower. Sea and lake ice open or close routes, make ice roads and set the hunting seasons. Frozen ground limits farming, building and burial, and its thaw can bring structures down and release what it held. Glaciers advance and retreat.

governs.title: Weather of Its Own
governs.text: Valleys, lakes, forests and cities make their own climates, and change where people settle, what they grow and what makes them sick.
